TITLE: Tailgate entry to site - poor attitude
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A Transit connect approached the site gate, buzzed the control room and after a conversation with the shift operator it was concluded that the person was at the wrong site and should be next door at the cement factory.

5 min later the Transit Connect appeared and parked to the side of the main gate. After approx 10 mins a contractor who is erecting a new fence arrived at site and drove to the barrier to card in. At this point the Transit drove immediately behind the fencing contractor and tail gated them into the site, by-passing security.

Uniper colleague immediately left the control room to challenge the driver of the transit connect who had followed the fencing contractor and parked close to them. The first person Uniper colleague saw was the fencing contractor leaving their vehicle. They were asked who the person was in the Transit connect and they said they didn't know.

Uniper colleague approached the driver to ask who they were, why they'd tailgated through and who they were here to see.

They told me their Manager had told them to do it. Asked who their manager was and who they were here to see. They didn't know either but said they were here to wok with the fencing contractor. The person was extremely aggressive and confrontational. They were asked to remain in their van whilst Uniper colleague spoke to the contractor. It transpired the individual was here to work with them and was an agency temp. Due to the poor attitude displayed from arriving at site when engaged and the security breach. Requested that the contract company removed the individual from site.

TITLE: PSO - U3 HP Shaft Position Indication Found Reading Off Scale
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The EC&I team were Investigating an oil leak on U3 HP Shaft position Differential Expansion probe.  It is standard practice to look at the current reading and note any standing alarms before any work is done.  The module was reading -1.25mm hard off scale.  There were no plant alarms standing.  Trending the value on the Ovation DCS revealed that the HP Shaft position had been reading off scale since 22/10/2021, just over 1 year.  Since this date, the generating unit has run many times with no accurate visibility of the turbine shaft position.  It was found that the alarms were not enabled in the measurement module.

TITLE: Welding rods fell from tool bag whilst walking up HRSG internal stairs.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Location: HRSG U71 Approx. 5m Level 

Incident :
-	Altrad Welder intend to walk up towards 27m Level to undertake works on Vent Valve Station. 
-	As welder walking on 2nd flight of stairs (Approx. 5m level), with his Tool & Equipment bag in his hand, he slightly stumbled (No loss of balance/ fallen) 
-	TIG Welding Rods fell down (slipped) from his T&E bag and showered to the lower level near the lift well. No Person injured. Majority of rods fell onto scaffold (crash deck) 
-	Asked with Welder was okay, removed rods from scaffold, informed to dispose of rods, explained why his method was incorrect for taking T&E to the work area. Highlighted quick preventative measures. 
-	
Potential Cause: 
-	Lack of awareness 
-	Welding rod cap ends not taped / secured. Welder to confirm if he was aware. 
-	Inadequate Tool Bags issued to Personnel 
-	Weight loading of bag – the bag was heavy upon checking – maybe caused a slight stumble 
-	Tool bag not zipped up (even if it was zipped up the tool bag is too small for TIG welding rods. Wrong Tool bag to carry rods. 
-	Welder tried to lift all equipment in one hand – Welding PPE (screen mask) & Tool bag.

To be assigned to Project Team

TITLE:
61BMA / BFB breaker closed when it shouldn't have.
Extended 31/05 see comments
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A fault on a separate CB required the 61BFB board to be switched out of service. This required changing the 61BMA board over from BFB board supply to BFA board supply. I opened the BFB / BMA circuit breaker and the BFA / BMA circuit breaker did not close on auto (as I believe it should have). Rather than close it, we awaited the standby diesel generator to cut in and take the board and back-sync the BMA board onto the BFA board. Once synchronised, the standby diesel generator shut down as expected. We were then just assessing what further actions were required on the BFB board, when the BFB / BMA circuit breaker closed automatically when it shouldn't have. This commoned up two supplies through the BMA board and two separate 11kv feeds which should not be allowed.

TITLE: U6 CW pump 2 motor testing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An LWC (2023/00538) was prepared for electrical testing of HV apparatus, U6 CW pump 2 motor. The motor was in its service position with the 415V motor heater connected. The motor HV supply cable was disconnected, isolated and earthed at the unit board with a PFW (2023/00517) prepared to reconnect the motor waiting to be issued. 

No safety precautions were attached to the LWC to prevent the motor being energized prior to or during the test, where direct contact with HV conductors would have been required, well within the approved safety distance for 11KV apparatus.

This was discovered when the CP presented his MWO to carry out the testing at the permit office.

TITLE: Removal of Waste from CDC site non-compliance
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Re-power project Trant Engineering additional work scope on behalf of EDF to remove old transformer bunds BHT03 and BHT05 waste.
EDF via email 24/03/2023 issued waste collection note to Uniper project team as documentary evidence to be added to project handover documentation of which was in addition to Hitachi (main contractor work scope).
On review of information project team had a meeting on the 04/04/2023 CDC Environmental officer to determine that project teams understanding was correct, the process had not been followed and that the documentation was non compliant for the reasons given below prior to issuing response to EDF.

Waste collection note issued is non-compliant for the following reasons: 
•	The collection and delivery addresses are to be in full including post codes
•	SIC code 3511 is missing
•	Producer (Uniper) has not signed the document and the declaration which has been ticked should be a declaration for the producer (Uniper) to sign (Appears that waste has been removed from CDC site without signed authorisation from Uniper representative as per agreed process).
•	Tonnage is not acceptable as 1 load as there are 2 EWC codes 17.01.01 and 17.05.04 in which Uniper require separate tonnage per code 

In addition Uniper have checked the waste carrier license 401 5100 30 and confirm license is still valid. Prior to waste being removed from Uniper CDC site Uniper should of received completed waste classification forms (WM3 assessments) for the 2 different wastes. As the EWC codes are mirror codes and have been deemed as non-hazardous by Trant Uniper require analysis data i.e. copy of test results to demonstrate non-hazardous waste. This information should have been provided to Uniper for review and acceptance prior to any waste being removed from site as per agreed process, this does not appear to have happened and a synergi case has been raised.

Response sent to EDF 04/04/2023 to provide the correct documentation and carry out an investigation with Trant Engineering and to provide an update to enable Uniper to complete the investigation.

TITLE: Dropped Object from Height causing injury
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During welding works inside the Can sections for the new stack a welder was working using magnets to secure his welding blanket to the side walls of the can sections.  His trailing light lead caught around one of the magnets and pulled it off causing it to fall down to the level below.  The distance travelled is approx 3.5 mtrs.  The weight of the magnet is approx 300gms.  Un be known to the welder at the higher level there was another welder on the level below directly in line.  the line of sight was blocked due to the welding blanket being in the position that it was.  The magnet fell and struck the welder below near to the crown of his head.  Colleagues immediately called for the first Aid and a dressing was applied to stem any bleeding.  Client was notified  immediately and all other notifications sent within the golden hour.  The IP was taken to the hospital where he was checked for concussion and glue applied to the laceration.  The IP has returned to work this morning.

TITLE: Blowdown Cooling System Control Panel Door Almost Fell Off Last Working Hinge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The blowdown cooling system had stopped working during the heavy rain and is required to cool the blowdown before discharge to sea. The panel door for the control system has been broken since 2018 (21295453) and not repaired so assumed water ingress had caused the system to trip. The panel door is held shut with gaffer tape, but we assumed this was to try to keep the door shut and water-tight. The gaffer tape was cut to access the panel and upon opening the door it nearly fell off the 1 remaining hinge keeping the door in place. The other 2 hinges have clearly failed in the past as not fixed to the door anymore.
This is a heavy stainless-steel door and could have caused serious injury if it had fully detached.
There have been multiple defects raised for this door, yet it's not been fully repaired (21295453, 21312566, 21422651, 21452022)

TITLE: PSNH - U3 A SSFP started unexpectedly
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst de-earthing / de-isolating U3 A SSFP, the pump started unexpectedly. The 11kv breaker was first removed from earth by tripping the breaker mechanically. The 11kv breaker was then removed from earth position, de-isolated and placed back in the cubicle and racked into the service position. The breaker selector was then switched from the OFF position to the REMOTE position. The mechanical and LV isolations were de-isolated and pre start checks carried out. The liquid reg Lram was raised and lowered to ensure control, at the same time the oil pump was turned to remote in the switchroom and the oil pump started straight away. The operative made their way round to the A SSFP to leak check the oil system. When the operative got to the oil pump he found the SSFP was running and fully in service. Contact was made with the control room to find out who had started the pump, the reply was nobody. The pump was then taken out of service immediately. EC&I and Turbine team were both made aware so the cause of the unexpected start could be investigated.

TITLE: Water shot incident
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On March 3rd 05:45 hrs, right after the feed tank change over from T-303 (crude mix: Doba 40.69%, Dar 34.35%, Nile 24.95%) to T-301 (crude mix: Nile 22.28%, Doba 73.50%, Dar 4.24%) both units had to be shut down due to a water shot.  
 
Following the tank feed switching operation the operations team noticed increased levels on back pressure in the Flash column, which could lead to an activation of  automatic trip sequence shutting down the crude feed pump (P-001), all other main equipment will follow to shut down after trip sequence. Due to this and to avoid further process and plant safety and potential H&S problems both units taken to  shut down. There was no loss of production as it happened during start up process. 
 

The CPUs are prepared as per design to take up to 3% suspended water but not to process free water, this is perceived as the main risk for this type of events. Similar events had occurred only 3 times in the asset lifetime, including this one. One of them was automatic trip due higher P in the Flash column. 

The most likely scenario in case of not addressing this situation in time is would be a pop up of the Pressure Safety Valve (PSV) in the Flask Column. In this case the affected unit will suffer unplanned unavailability for the reinstallation of the PSV. In case of additional failure of the PSV, the failure could lead to a malfunction in the Flash column potentially leading to release of vapours (depending on where within the flask columns the failure materializes it might lead to release of vapours, crude etc).  

The crude feed tank that was being used , T-301,  had been last operated by Uniper Ops team, on February 24th, due to vessel discharge operations was. In this case the available time for tank preparation was sufficient.

TITLE: Excessive oil from drained pipework
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
ST Clutch Lube Oil supply pipe weld was commenced on Sunday morning 30th august 2020. 
On cutting the existing pipe the Doosan Tech saw more oil than he was expecting draining under head from the stub pipe he had cut, not under pressure just weiring over. 
He stopped work ,informed us and we went to investigate. 
There was quite a bit of oil in the gallery under the grating. We applied a spill kit and requested Wayne Chandler to assist cleaning it up with spill pads. 
There was about 10 litres of oil possibly that we mopped up and it stopped flowing from the stub.
We conducted a job stop and meeting with GE supervisor. jacking oil work was suspended while we established a cause.

 The reason for the oil draining from the pipework was the fact that the bearing pedestals had filled with oil because of the jacking oil being put into service constantly. The level would reach the supply pipework internally to the pedestal.
This then ran down the SUPPLY pipework, filling the blanked and previously drained line back to the tank.. 
It was drain under head only and a gentle weiring from the stub. It would drain and stop . when jacking oil back in service a little bit more would drain.

We fitted a drain hose to the cut stub pipe and this was placed into an IBC to collect any oil. Permit for Clutch supply pipe weld cancelled.
 Monday 31st August the line was drained at the supply blank and the blank removed . Lube oil pumps isolated and PFW issued to weld flange onto stub after line proved drained again..
 
 History;
Supply pipework drained and Lube oil blank fitted under PFW 2020/00819 on 01/08/2020 and entered into blanks register.
Drain /return lines back to tank remained available throughout.
This was the basis for our Clutch weld job.
Clutch weld job PFW2020/ 00945 issued 15/08/2020(proved drained) work allowed to commence 30/08/2020 (drained line now contained oil).

Excessive oil from drained pipework. ST Clutch Lube Oil supply pipe weld was commenced on Sunday morning 30th august 2020. 
On cutting the existing pipe the Doosan Tech saw more oil than he was expecting draining under head from the stub pipe he had cut, not under pressure just weiring over. 
He stopped work ,informed us and we went to investigate. 
There was quite a bit of oil in the gallery under the grating. We applied a spill kit and requested Wayne Chandler to assist cleaning it up with spill pads. 
There was about 10 litres of oil possibly that we mopped up and it stopped flowing from the stub.
We conducted a job stop and meeting with GE supervisor. jacking oil work was suspended while we established a cause.

 The reason for the oil draining from the pipework was the fact that the bearing pedestals had filled with oil because of the jacking oil being put into service constantly. The level would reach the supply pipework internally to the pedestal.
This then ran down the SUPPLY pipework, filling the blanked and previously drained line back to the tank.. 
It was drain under head only and a gentle weiring from the stub. It would drain and stop . when jacking oil back in service a little bit more would drain.

We fitted a drain hose to the cut stub pipe and this was placed into an IBC to collect any oil. Permit for Clutch supply pipe weld cancelled.
 Monday 31st August the line was drained at the supply blank and the blank removed . Lube oil pumps isolated and PFW issued to weld flange onto stub after line proved drained again..
 
 History;
Supply pipework drained and Lube oil blank fitted under PFW 2020/00819 on 01/08/2020 and entered into blanks register.
Drain /return lines back to tank remained available throughout.
This was the basis for our Clutch weld job.
Clutch weld job PFW2020/ 00945 issued 15/08/2020(proved drained) work allowed to commence 30/08/2020 (drained line now contained oil).

TITLE: SC20 PCC Low Voltage Switchroom Incident
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An EMI operative was glanding and terminating a cable. The cable outer insulation had been removed to expose the wire armour, the previous day (08/02).
As part of the preparation (09/02), the operative laid out the cable to check its identification. Due to the location of the gland plate and the termination point, approximately 4m of cable was laid out. The operative laid the cable out, on the floor to the wall end of the PCC and was returning to the works location, when he heard an arcing sound. The operative turned around to see the cable sparking between the switchroom wall and a cabinet.
The operative called to his work partner (located on a different part of the PCC) and both operatives moved away and called for assistance.

No injuries sustained.

TITLE: Water shot incident
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On May 14th at 21:45 hrs, Both CPUs were running from T-302 (crude mix: Doba 96.88%, Dar 1.21%, Nile 1.91%) and panel operator found feed pump discharge and column pressure increasing beyond control, both units forced to shut down suspecting water shot.

During above the operations team noticed increased levels on back pressure in the Flash column, which could lead to an activation of  automatic trip sequence shutting down the crude feed pumps (P-1-001 & P-2-001), all other main equipment will follow to shut down after trip sequence. Due to this and to avoid further process and plant safety and potential H&S problems both units taken to  shut down. There was a loss of production of 6 hours 45 minutes in CPU 1 and 7 hours 35 minutes in CPU 2. 


The CPUs are prepared as per design to take up to 3% suspended water but not to process free water, this is perceived as the main risk for this type of events. Similar events had occurred on 3rd March 2021. One of them was automatic trip due higher P in the Flash column. 

The most likely scenario in case of not addressing this situation in time is would be a pop up of the Pressure Safety Valve (PSV) in the Flask Column. In this case the affected unit will suffer unplanned unavailability for the reinstallation of the PSV. In case of additional failure of the PSV, the failure could lead to a malfunction in the Flash column potentially leading to release of vapours (depending on where within the flask columns the failure materializes it might lead to release of vapours, crude etc).

TITLE: Spindle on isolation valve installed wrong way round
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When performing isolation of the HP glycol pumps one of the isolation valves used for isolation did not isolate as expected, it was found in a closed position and opened for the isolation, it should have been the other way around. 

This was due to the spindle having been attached 90 degrees the wrong way to the valve, then when the handle was attached to the spindle although lined up correctly gave the appearance to the operator that the valve was open when really it was shut and vice versa.

This was picked up during the isolation process by the SAP, if this had not been identified it could have resulted in someone working on a pressurised system at around 3 bar. It also meant that during operations the equipment had been running without protection of the downstream pipework and lean glycol tank from over-pressurisation.

TITLE: (Outage) Unit 2 cooling tower 415v 'A' side ACB fault
CASE_DESCRIPTION: unit 2 cooling tower 415v 'A' side ACB, stating the ACB was faulty, required repair & was racked out in preparation for repair. On initial inspection the faulty ACB was in fact in the 'B' side of U2 cooling tower 415v board. Investigation found the two 'ACB's' had been swapped over the night before to enable supplies to be re-instated onto the 'A' side of the cooling tower board. Since the faulty 'A' side ACB was now 'isolated' the 'Castel' key could be removed

TITLE:
SSoW
Electricity - electric shock
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A request was made for maintenance works to be carried out on “SM Plant Effluent Sump Pump “B” 415v Contactor”.  The SAP believed that the request was for the WTP Effluent Sump Pump “B” 415v Contactor”.

This misunderstanding came about because the long text on the maintenance order only stated “Effluent Sump Pump “B” 415v Contactor”.

Due to the Long Text wording (associated with the functional location) being poorly described, the SAP was not directed to the correct item of plant to isolate.  The high level functional location description is however correct.

As the works preparer drilled down to the specific functional location, some of the preceding text disappears and leaves the Functional Location long text description information too generic, and in this case very open to interpretation.

The Craft Team member was unsure about the location of the source of supply quoted on their permit and rightly checked the location prior to starting work to find the isolation did not tie up with the works requested.

TITLE: Lifting of a load without a tag line fitted.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A crane lift, of  sheeting panels onto U42 were witnessed without a tag line fitted. This caused the panels on both occasions to spin and bump into the side of the access platform and structure. No injury or damaged sustained.
Several staff members witnessed the incident and intervened.
The panel was blowing about and started to spin. The driver in the cherry picker moved his basket in to the panel to stop it spinning around so he could control it and place the panel where it needed to go. Whilst several of the witnesses set off  to speak to the working party, they started lifting another panel so they decided to let them finish. As the panel was being lifted they noticed that there wasn’t a tagline attached. Again, the panel started blowing about and was slammed in to the steel work of the enclosure, the panel struck the steel work another 2 times before the driver in the cherry picker could control it. Two of witnesses went and spoke to the rigging crew and supervisor on the ground who were stood watching the lift, they were asked to use a tag line, which was about 2m away. The lifting party were reminded that if it’s too windy, don’t carry out the lift.

TITLE: Undertaking work on valve removal and replacement to the HCL line and storage tank within the bunded area.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The subject of LONE WORKING was brought to the attention of Carl Newcombe ( UNIPER ) by the Contractors (Phoenix) who had observed a UNIPER person lone working on an aspect of the HCL system which involved breaking into system within the confines of its Bund. 

I realise on initial review and discussion that:

•	He was wearing the correct PPE for the works.
•	Had a Safety Document issued by the SAP which had ensured safety from the system was in place, with WO and RAMS which apparently covered the work.
•	Person involved had a radio on the understanding that this was his means of communication with the Control Rm in the event of distress, injury or other problem.

Although all these points were in place on review of the RAMS; 

•	The RAMS generated by Eclipse on SAP did state No Lone Working at the very end of the Risk assessment.

What is the interpretation that should be followed when it states No Lone Working on the RAMS. 
My current thought is what passed without event on the day in question, next time might not and being reliant on a radio may not offer the timely response required.

TITLE: Steam Turbine Trip on Run up
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On run up this morning the steam turbine tripped at 44Hz due to low reheat steam temperature. Steam turbine had to slowed using the E shaft vac valve. On re run off the steam turbine program the step sequence faulted at step 18,This has led to believe to be the start up device. This is infact the steam turbine program looking for X5 which is lost, the Start up device appears to be a red herring. We found that even if the steam turbine is selected to fast from a trip it still looks for X5 positive which is not the same criteria of a HOF start. Hence the start up device is not the issue. Defects have been entered for the reheat thermocouples reading low.

TITLE: Unauthorised crossing of a fixed no entry barrier around Unit 41 transformer on Sync Comp Project.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The supervisor (who had constructed this barrier previously) asked the individual (a Siemens engineer) as to why he was inside the barriered area. He claimed to have permission from his employer and had been issued with a permit.  The supervisor challenged this, knowing that the area was out of bounds to everyone and the access gate was still locked. The supervisor told the engineer to vacate the area immediately, and after a bit of hesitance, the engineer climbed over the fixed barrier and exited the area.
The incident was immediately report to Uniper and Siemens management.

TITLE: Main Gas Valve would not open.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A recent Gas detection panel fault had closed the sites main Gas valve 10EKG70AA001 on protection. During the unit start up 3 attempts were made to start the GT for it’s DP run scheduled for 15:00 – 21:00. Each attempt failed due to time out of the fuel gas program as a result of 10EKG70AA001 not opening in time. On the 3rd start attempt, the valve was locally observed to see what was happening. It became apparent that the valve was trying to run open but not moving more than a fraction. Numerous attempts were made to drive the valve open, both electrically from the DCS, locally and manually using the handwheel. It was concluded the valve was either mechanically jammed or pressure locked. After some discussion, the decision was made to try and reduce the pressure upstream of the valve by venting off gas from the pre-heater. This was successful and allowed the valve to be re-opened.

TITLE: U1 Boiler HP Sootblower Control Valve 255.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Monday 27th September at approx 0830, a Permit For Work ROMP ( Restoration of Motive Power) was issued from the Outage permit for work office to allow the set-up of limits and stroking of pneumatic valve 255 following outage works.  At the time of issue the boiler was being set up for a Hydraulic test.  As per normal procedure and prior to the hydraulic, all issued docs were checked and any relevant safety documents that could affect the hydraulic were suspended.  Between the times of the check of the issued documents and start of the boiler hydraulic, the ROMP for valve 255 was issued without the issuing SAP making the connection to it being affected by the boiler hydraulic.  The CP who collected the Romp proceeded to his point of work, made the air supply available and started to stroke the valve from the local junction box.  As the valve opened there was a release of pressure within the process pipework, which was 'quite loud' and caused vibration within the pipework.  This startled the CP and he proceeded to shut the control air valve immediately.   The CP reported straight to the Outage duty SAP who attended the point of work and realised the ROMP should not have been in force during the boiler hydraulic test.  The ROMP was suspended and working party withdrawn.   

The PFW ROMP specifically stated no access to the process side of the control valve / system, so the CP and working party were not at risk from the process medium.

5) CPU-2 ESD activated.

7) OSC Ramasamy from Refinery arrived at site and assessed the situation for any emergency help.

TITLE: WTP Effluent Tank Leak in to Bund.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Shift team received a radio message from Kaefer at approx. 15:00 11/10/21 reporting a very high level in WTP Effluent Tanks bund. Shift team immediately investigated and confirmed high level. No evidence to suggest the leak had breached the bund and no evidence of any release to ground. Effluent systems made unavailable and pumps electrically isolated. Area was then barriered off to restrict access. Potential leak source from flanged joint on 09SDATK080 identified, tank level  below level this joint at time of issue and leakage had stopped . Contents of bund sampled and were approx. 11pH. 09SXSUV001 and 002 closed as a precaution. Shift Team called Veolia Emergency response to arrange for tanker to empty bund contents. Shift team continuously monitored bund level using CCR cameras and carried out regular inspections of location to ensure no increase in level or leakage from bund until Ancorra attended site 10:30 12/10/21 to empty bund contents. Bund emptied of contents by 14:00 12/10/21.

TITLE: Steam Turbine Trip, Following Trip Testing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Gas turbine overspeeds, steam turbine overspeeds & steam turbine HP stop valve/governor valve tested successfully. Plant was stable and running at 400MW.
12:09hrs TST IP SV + CV Left FAIL 18MAB11EA121. Whereby, IP steam turbine governor valve closed fully, but the IP stop valve remained in intermediate mode (18MAB11AA001). Result was worsened vacuum >250mbar causing the steam turbine to trip (18MAX43EZ903_XU51). REMIT call submitted to Trading approximately 12:10hrs. Load dropped to SEL, drum levels controlled, air cooled condenser demin sprays put into service and sequencer selected to bypass. Grid were called to inform them of the situation.
By 12:17hrs, SEL was achieved. Due to standby to bypass being selected, gas turbine continued to deload.
At about 12:28hrs, Trading called requesting a REMIT update: 70MW from 12:30hrs to 13:30hrs. Then, between 13:30 and 13:43hrs increase load from 70 to 240MW. Remain at SEL until 15:00hrs.
Grid called and updated.
~ 13:34hrs programme device became disabled on the steam turbine and was manually given an ON command. Steam turbine became to ramp up from 70 to 240MW.
Steam turbine, at the time of writing is stable, and control valve stresses are improving (26 & 68% for HP and IP valves respectively.)

TITLE: U4 main coalescer vent found open causing small (10-20L) oil spill.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On Friday morning, a report was received to the outage office that there was oil dripping from the Coalescer drain separator vessel.  On investigation it was found that the Coalescer vent valve had been opened slightly.  The oil issuing into the Coalscer drain had eventually overcome the drains separator, and spilled a small amount of oil onto the basement floor.  The vent was closed immediately upon discovery.  It is not known how long, when or for what reason the vent was opened, but it is presumed it had been unintentionally knocked by a person or object at some point that morning.  There was no operational reason to operate or move the valve, and no-one was in the vicinity of the Coalscer when the open vent was discovered and closed.   The jacking oil pumps, oil tank and Coalescer were all available for normal service and at NWP.

TITLE: U4 Kue grit blast waste, failure to segregate waste as per agreed method resulting in additional work to properly segregate waste.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Kue a sub contractor to Doosan undertook grit blast of the primary and secondary platens in U4 boiler. Agreed method was to sweep and bag waste and transport to 'duct bags' on pallets to be segregated on site, this was part of method statement and confirmed again just prior to work. Work was undertaken from Friday 20/5/22 to Sunday 22/5/22. Altrad provided resource to collect the waste on pallets and to remove and store onsite. The work area was inspected at the end of the job, the main focus was the prep, however it was noted that the scaffold was clean, free of waste grit and the when asked if the plastic sheeting had been removed we were told "yes" Kue also made a point to say that the Altrad resource had been very helpful, as the Altrad resource had been set up specifically to remove the waste it was assumed that this therefore had gone well. Based on inspection of the work area, the Kue paper work was signed by Chris Onions, both for completion of the shot blast areas and that the work area was clean and tidy. Kue left site on Sunday 22/5/22.  

On Monday 23/5/22 the Environmental team enquired where the waste was stored as it could not be found. On enquiring with the Altrad resource, they confirmed that there had been no waste generated. It was at this point that it was realised that Kue had not followed the agreed method for waste removal and had undertaken a different method. On inspection of the ash hopper it became apparent that it contained the waste shot.

An enquiry with Kue via Doosan, it was confirmed that not waste was collected and bagged, it instead was swept off the sheeted scaffold directly into the ash hopper. No waste had left site, no waste had entered any other skip/bin and the total amount of waste was 4 tonnes. The waste is therefore contained in the ash hopper and will be removed by shovel and bag and disposed of as per original plan.

TITLE: Draw Pit Access Incorrect Procedures for Work
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
I received a phone call from Gary Polson Production Team Leader at approximately 12:10 p.m. 28 June 2022 informing me he had stopped a Trant Engineering  employee working on the Make Up Water and Purge Water project from working within a cable draw pit adjacent to the CDC cooling towers.

This system has not been Safety Rules Inclusion Certified (SRIC) as yet and is not part of the CDC systems as it is still under the Trant Engineering safety rules for construction.

This is an EDF CDM project and an investigation will be carried out by EDF Principal Contractor/Client in conjunction with their main Contractor Trant Engineering Ltd and Shaun McConnell Trant Engineering SHE advisor who attended site and is currently carrying out an investigation of which will be shared with Uniper
I attended the work area and discussed with Gary the concerns he had raised.

Points noted with Gary were, lack of barriers demarcating the work area, no safety A frame or harness in place, no second man above ground and no gas monitor being worn. Gary pointed out that when the Trant Engineering employee stood up in the pit his head and shoulders were above the surface of the draw pit.
Please note this draw pit has not been deemed as a Confined space .


I contacted Trant Engineering Civils Manager and asked him to attend site immediately of which he did, discussion with myself and Civils Manager and points noted agreed as per next paragraph

Lack of barriers demarcating the work area, no safety A frame or harness in place, no second man above ground, gas monitor not being worn and 4 inches of water in the draw pit.
Trant Engineering 755-TEL-XX-XX-PL-Z-0009 – Emergency Response Plan not being adhered to.
Trant Engineering 755-TEL-XX-XX-MS-C-0057 Rescue Plan not being adhered to.


Civils Manager instructed his employees to  replace the covers and stop work.

Please see attached photographs

TITLE: Emergency Evacuation Test
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Persons Involved:
J Plage - Gatehouse
A Black - 3rd floor
M Williams - Control Room

Work halted on fire panel and system returned to normal operating mode.

Timeline:

11:00am - Site evacuation alarm sounded.
11:02 - Day team mustered in room adjacent to control room. 3rd floor confirmed clear.
11:03am - Security team deployed barrier to avoid unwanted access to site.
11:05am - One person arrived at gatehouse without fob. Security logged this and manually entered him as mustered. Dragon building confirmed clear.
11:09am - P Sloan assigns himself as Muster Controller. N Evans assisted.
11:12am - Electronic record of personnel on site printed. 3 persons unaccounted for.
11:14am - Role call taken at evacuation point - 3 persons unaccounted for present (fobs not picked up by scanner).

Comments:

Interrogation of system confirmed all persons had actually evacuated by 11:10am. Shift team were unable to silence the evacuation alarm in the control room which could have adversely affected comms during a genuine incident. Because of the positioning of the PPBoard, day team members were not visible to the shift TL.

TITLE: U1 61 Sootblower.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst carrying out scaffolding to the full length of U1 No61 Sootblower, the opposing Sootblower on U2 (No62) went into service.  The operatives were scaffolding around the drive end of U1 61, so were in close proximity to U2 No62.  This particular style of Sootblower (of which there are at least 8 on section 2 per unit) have a section of unguarded shaft on the side of the drive end.  The Operatives were in close proximity to the unguarded rotating shaft and were installing supports directly below it.  The operative immediately reported this to their supervisor and the working party withdrew from the area.
There has been an assessment of the same design of Sootblower across unit 1 & 2 and all Sootblowers of this type have an approx 30" section of exposed shaft, of which at least 4 are at an accessible height on a walkway adjacent to a main stairwell.
The shafts do spin relatively slowly
Please note these are original design Sootblowers that have been installed and used for the station life, and I understand they have never been guarded.

TITLE: Noise from HRSG roof, potential for complaints from neighbours.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Approaching site by road I noticed a larger than usual steam plume above the HRSG. Unit had started at 04:00, so by 07:00 all steam venting should have been complete. Loud venting noise could be heard from site car park, increasing in volume as I made my way through the outage car park to the site perimeter (See attached video). Since noise of this type lead to a an enquiry from a neighbour on return to service from the HE outage I contacted CCR who carried out a plant inspection, inspected DCS screens and found 18LBA50AA211 ST drain valve open. Valve was interlocked and held open by DCS software. DCS engineer is investigating, but valve is now closed and noise has gone. No external complaints have been received as of 07:45

TITLE: Rotor stand up work: lifting hook slipped out from the hook frame
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While installing the special upending lifting nut to the rotor, the support ring from the nut slipped off.

Why did it happen: As it turns out the crane couldn´t drive far enough to the end of the GT hall, this creates a forward momentum to the device (yellow ring on the picture). While the installation process our Rotor specialist need to open the locking plates from the device to continue the installation process. While removing those locks the forward momentum simply pulls away the device and left the nut unsupported. 
After that the nut where supported by a forklift, the installing device where brought back in place and installing process continued without any further problems.

Conclusion: in future the thread dimensions should be taken and a certain length must be defined before opening locking plates.

no damage or injury occurred during this Event

Shutdown applied to turbine, turbine was then reset & a pilot ESV start was selected.
Issue may have been compounded by Turbine tripping off barring / steam barring.

TITLE: Hire Car Loss of Acceleration when moving on to A1 carriageway with traffic
CASE_DESCRIPTION: While I was pulling out of a layby in a company provided hire car (supplied via Hertz) I attempted to accelerate to join the traffic in a safe manner.  I had waited for a suitable gap in the traffic and then proceeded to accelerate.  The car initially accelerated normally to 20mph and then accelerated at a significantly reduced level.  This was concerning as the gap in traffic I had moved out in to was OK for a car able to accelerate to 70mph normally but wasn't large enough to allow for reduced acceleration.  This caused the vehicle behind to brake hard to avoid colliding with my vehicle.  I was able to over come the issue by manually shifting the gears and slowly accelerating until the car reached normal road speeds; the car then appeared to recover from the error and was able to drive normally again.  I then left the dual carriageway at the next exit and altered my route home to avoid busy roads. The car was fully automatic petrol car and had been performing correctly up to his point.

TITLE: Thick black smoke from CPU-1 Furnace stack
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On 4th March 2021, 23:30 hrs the VTTI operations team observed black smoke from the stack of CPU-1 furnace (tag no. ME-1-001) (see Annex 1 “Annex 1_CPU-1 Furnace stack smoke email VTTI_20210304.pdf”). As the thick smoke was continuously coming out the operators stopped the furnace at 23:45 hrs and the unit was taken into long circulation. At 02:30 hours on 5th March 2021 the CPU-1 was put under short circulation (see Annex 2 “Annex 2_CPU Log Sheet as of 4th March 2021”).
The following day, the furnace control system (BMS) was restarted by Uniper E&I Maintenance team for a default reset of error values. After this CPU-1 furnace was re-started 2 times on a trial basis, checking that continuous white smoke was coming from the stack. Subsequently firing of ME-1-001 was stopped waiting for further investigation, with the final objective of finding the root cause of the incident. For the investigation it was decided to get support from specialized 3rd parties such as Harris Pye (HP) and Bureau Veritas(BV).
In total because of this incident CPU-1 was down ca. 30 days from March 4th, 2021 23:30 hrs until April 3rd 14:00 hrs.

TITLE: CPU-1 P-1-007 Suction piping chemical injection leak
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On 16th February ’20 at early morning around 0300 hrs. the Field operator during his rounds at CPU-1 noticed fumes and HFO leaking through the insulation cladding of the suction loop from Pump-1-007 (Flash column HFO R/D pump) suction side. Field operator immediately informed at the CCR and the pump was stopped immediately, and the plant taken to ESD, pump isolated & depressurized. DNO tag was provided for suction and discharge block valves. The area was cordoned off. The HFO leakage was about 50 liters but that was onto the pump skid tray, and the leak didn’t splash or spread out elsewhere. There was no personnel hurt, no contamination, as it was contained and no property damage as well. Initial findings on opening up the insulation cladding; On the 2‘‘ branch piping where Chemical SR1394 was being injected on a trial basis there was pin hole discovered, which was the source of the leak, and later after the system was cooled, drained out completely and inerted, the spool piece was removed and found that there was heavy corrosion on the internal base of the spool. Suspecting the pitted hole due to excessive corrosion contributed by the chemical being injected. Prior to start of use, it was confirmed and verified by the vendor that it was compatible with MS, CS & SS, but in reality it seemed that chemical was not compatible with CS at all, and had severe effects on CS.

TITLE: Unauthorised operation of part of a safety system.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Work had been completed on the A-site fire system, and the system had been charged and was holding at 11 bar with out the need for the jockey pumps to cut in.
At 08.26 shortly after a Hydrant key had been collected for CW cleaning works, Jockey pump 2 cut in followed quickly by the electric fire pump.
It was assumed that the guys using the fire system on the CW  works had caused this.
When checking the A-site fire system @ ~09:30 the drain on the fire system manifold adjacent to block house 3a was found open.
This valve had not been open overnight and no permission had been given for the valve to be opened.
Taking into account the amount of water around the drain valve it is thought that it was opened at around the time the electric fire pump cut in.

TITLE: Station and Unit Auxiliary steam header over pressurisation.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 1 desync 2025hrs, Unit 4 sync 2207hrs, Unit 2 desync 2255hrs.
At 2254hrs Aux Boilers 210, 240 & 250 tripped due to a fleeting gas detector (Steam Generator 2 Gas Detector).
Until the Boiler system and gas slam shut valve could be reset the aux steam header was supplemented from Units 1 & 2, manually,  via SVAPCV019. This initially resulted in an momentary over pressurisation of the Auxiliary Steam Headers up to18Bar, (0*-SVA-025-PT).  Unit 3 Auxiliary Steam Header was isolated and depressurised for outage and so unaffected.
The Aux Steam header then dropped to 2 Bar before Aux Boilers 220 and 230 began loading enough to raise the pressure.
This resulted in the condenser pressures of Unit 1 reaching 165mBar and Unit 2 301mBar due to low gland steam pressures. Unit 4 vacuum was unaffected.
The Gas Treatment Plant was being started at the time of the trip, which required some venting of the compressor HP suction drum V403, and the wind was from the west (this may or may not relate to the gas detector trip).

The Unit Auxiliary Steam Header Safety Valves PSV003 are rated to lift at 18Bar according to the P&ID.

TITLE: Unanticipated effect from altered Operator set point
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An initial problem was detected with the GRUs where they were quickly dumping >6m3 hour of cold teg into the regen units on start up, which if wet could lead to a pressure trip. A modification was prepared for tuning out some poor control on the flow limiter on the stripping column.  However, it was not implemented because on closer inspection, the Rich TEG buffer vessel level Operator-adjustable set point was sitting at a low level.  Increasing the set point from 380 mm to 500 mm smoothed the start up process and prevented the pressure trips.

After a period of time, Operators detected that during the shut down of the GRUs, the TEG HP pumps were repeatedly turning on and off.  Investigation identified that this was because the auto-changeover setpoint of 1m3/hr was now being matched by the flow of Rich TEG from the buffer tank due to the changed setpoint (as described above).

There was no safety consequence to the pumps repeatedly changing over.  However, there was a potential plant damage risk.  Hence, this observation has been raised to determine any additional learning relating to the sites control of modification set points, including operator adjustable set points.

TITLE: Wrongly prioritised alarm
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An alarm was discovered on unit 6 DCS linked to the Tantronic gas detection system. We often receive a lot of nuisance annunciations of this particular alarm due to low sample flows. On this occasion it was investigated and the same alarm was showing that there was a fault on the system (sample pump failure). This meant that there was no EV or SEV combustion ring gas detection and the alarm received was the same priority 3 alarm that you would receive for a low sample flow on one sample point.
A failure of a part of the gas detection system should give a more significant alarm.

TITLE: Underrated cutting/grinding disc for grinder
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A dip check by Kaefer & Uniper of Salko revealed that the speed rating of their cutting and grinding discs were not compatible with the speed rating of their angle grinder.
• 150mm Cutting/Grinding discs rated at 10,200 rpm Max.
• 125mm Angle grinder rated at11,000 rpm
The five inch angle grinders had been fitted with six inch guards, enabling incorrect discs to be fitted. Make sure the machine's speed is at or below the maximum operating speed of the wheel. Surpassing this rating risks not just wheel breakage but also the safety of the operative and adjacent personnel.

On 90/09/21 trailer attached to BM car to return to Tech Centre, visual checks carried out before departing although not on trailer chassis. BM stopped at Toddington service area on return journey and observed that nothing hanging from base of trailer. On parking trailer on slope outside CTF at tech centre trailer brake applied and car rolled forward to extend 'spring' on trailer, however, became apparent trailer brake not working. BM parked trailer inside CTF as is a flat area and no possibility of trailer rolling away once disconnected from vehicle.  T&M team informed of issue via email and CAT team asked to call Briggs to repair trailer (booked for Fri 17th Sept)

TITLE: GRU 30 incomplete combustion event and reboiler low pressure trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 28th February noticed puffs of black smoke being emitted from GRU 30 stack, not long after the Rich TEG feed had been introduced and on the following day the unit tripped on low reboiler pressure, again as the Rich TEG feed was being established.

The PI trend for the low pressure trip on the 1st March follows a very similar pattern to the trips observed in February & March 2020 and at the time wetter than normal Rich TEG was put forward as a possible explanation for a large spike in the reboiler pressure. However, the upstream GDU moisture analyser EKC10CQ001 wasn’t operating at the time which made this quite speculative.

One possible explanation for this could be the residual wetter than normal TEG held up in the contactors (approximately 14 m3) which would be transferred to the Rich Buffer tank in the subsequent withdrawals during which time it would be made partially drier by the incoming TEG although this would still have quite a high moisture content.

While the wet TEG theory remains far from conclusive it now has more credibility and GRU 30 was operated on the 2nd March with a Rich TEG feed which probably contained a more normal moisture content and no operating issues were observed.

TITLE: SIS trip GRU20 reboiler high pressure QCA20ZP004
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Regen 20 was up and running and the cooling air pressure to the combustion chamber (QCA20ZP004) had started to drop off. 
Caused by ice forming over the cooling fan vent mesh which requires removal by technician. 

On this occasion though, it was an unusually freezing cold wet night and when technician went to remove the ice from the mesh they inadvertently made it worse as they wiped water across the mesh and it instantly froze blocking off all the air flow which resulted in the trip.

TITLE: Risk of Pipe Breakage
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Risk of pipe breakage in the basement of the WSG substation in Rotterdam. 

The connection structure of the two recent incidents are identical. The construction consists of a weldolet welded to the DN500 discharge pipe with a front welding flange, a valve and a blanking plate at the end. In both cases the leakage was in the weldolet > DN25 pipe. This type of construction has been used in several places throughout the district heating system. 

The discovery of the leakage has been detected after it has been torn for approximately 85% to 90%.

Findings:
1. Vibrations have been present since construction. This has led to multiple leaks such as in the return system (temporary strainer). Vibration is still present despite modifications.
2. The construction of the connection constructions are heavy compared to the DN25 diameter of the split. 
3. Crack indication occurs first, then leakage and eventually the pipe could break off in the most extreme case.
4. Leaks are hardly ever observed.
5. There is no full security due to the lack of 24/7 staff on location. 

Conclusion:
Uniper runs an increased risk for an impending incident in the other connections in the district heating system.

TITLE: Coronavirus Close Contact Assessment breach of EGTL COVID-19 Procedure.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Friday 17th September it was reported that a GE/Fieldcore operative could not smell the wd40 he was using, as a precaution he took a LFT which proved positive, he left site in a controlled manner and the area sanitised, a close contact assessment completed. (He was a few days later confirmed positive by the official PCR).
3 operatives where identified and each had a LFT which all proved negative, they all had been double jabbed and were assessed able to carry on working as per Government advice.
However this against EGTL site procedure and against the instruction of the Grain Safety Team Leader who was contacted on A/L. The EGTL procedure insists that all Close Contacts should have been isolated until such time that the EGTL Appendix 9 RTW for Close Contacts had been completed. 
The Safety Team Leader did not find out until Tuesday 21st that the Close Contacts had been allowed to stay at work.
LFT have been conducted daily on the Close Contacts and surveillance and controls in place and negative results recorded.

As of this time no repeat has been reported. potential breakdown of new HTA Biocide to Ammonia suggested as possible Root Cause.

TITLE: Bus Collision with Car
CASE_DESCRIPTION: I got on the bus at the Crown Plaza hotel (Dusseldorf) to travel to the management conference evening event.  I sat on the bus, which was nowhere near full.  I had not immediately put on my seatbelt as I was expecting the rest of the seats to become occupied before the bus departed. Shortly after sitting down my phone rang.  I answered it.  The bus started moving and a couple of metres later came to an abrupt halt.  I did not have time to put on my seatbelt. I was propelled forward and hit my face on the seat in front of me.  There was some immediate pain but fortunately it was short lived.  The bus had collided with a car, which was why it stopped abruptly.  All bus passengers were moved onto another bus whereby I put on my seatbelt immediately!

TITLE: Review management of work system between Ops and Engineering and between the 5 Ops Shift Teams, with the aim of achieving consistency across the shift teams when assessing MO's and preparation of documents. In addition, investigate how to achieve a consistent standard of MO presented by engineering before placing on the weekly plan.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The following is an example of detail found on an MO and is an example that should never be allowed to happen: -

"While going through the plan today I noticed the above MO number already had a SAP decision on it, looking in enhancement it also had a Permit assigned to it – 2020/00406. 

As it looked like an older number I checked nisoft and this permit was “Not Issued” on 15/05/2020. 

I am concerned that we have received a MO on the plan that already has a safety decision applied along with a permit that is not ‘live’. I think the possibility of being able to re-using old MO’s needs investigating. I thought this was not possible. If it is then this has potentially serious consequences.

In this case the system has stopped any potential accidents as the MO could not be used with a cancelled/not issued document, however, If the original safety decision was at lower level such as a FWI and that MO was regurgitated but the plant/apparatus condition has since changed (therefore requiring precautions) it could prove to be more serious. As SAP’s we do not and can not check through every SAP decision that has already been made, some don’t even see this as they use GWOZ and only look at MO’s on the plan that are set to SRDR."

Questions I feel need answering are:
1. Who is capturing the volume of gaps in the standard of MO as there is no log book or day SAP in position.
2. What was captured in previous audits, regarding SAP MO's and documents, were any actions identified and carried out?
3. Discussion surrounding who and when a Safety Decision should be made to a MO and when is it suitable to place a document in 'mod' is being held across members of the Ops Team - should there be clarity from the management team so there is consistency?

TITLE: PSNH  - U3 re-heater Intercept valve tripping leading to r/htr safety valve 166 to lift.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On unit 3 run-up A1 Re-heater Intercept valve tripped and went undetected. The unit was synchronised and proceeded to load up, at approx. 440MW Hot Re-heater safety valve 166 lifted as a result of the intercept valve being tripped. Although the HP exhaust pressure was only 40 bar, indicating the safety valve had lifted “light” (there are also 4 other R/htr safety valves passing on this unit).
The unit load was reduced to 230MW initially thus reducing R/htr pressure and enable a gag to be installed, unsuccessful the load had to be reduced further to 20MW allowing successful fitting of the gag. Unit load was then returned back to full capacity. 
The problem of the tripping intercept valves on fast (5 minute) run-ups has been highlighted several times in the past and a previous OIT raised. Also, the turbine valve tripping isn’t highlighted significantly enough, meaning operators can miss this crucial problem.

TITLE: Operational Loss - U2 MBFP off barring
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst off load the MBFP tripped off barring and would not restart. The turbine proved to be tight and would not hand barr. The unit came off load at 23:00, MBFP on barring at 23:30. At 01:30 the bottom belt temperature suddenly dropped from 284 to 187 Oc , 5 minutes later the turbine tripped, no other operational activity was taking place at the time. The temperature continued to fall down to 95 Oc at 3:30 with the turbine still stationary. In an attempt to rectify the situation the condenser level was reduced and loop pipe drains opened. This increased the bottom belt temperature back up to 180 Oc at 05:00 and enabled the turbine to be hand barred half a turn. It appears a build up of condensate occurred within the bottom belt however investigations could not identify the cause of this . The turbine was shut down correctly, all drains checked in the correct position.

TITLE: Doosan employees found in Keafer scaffold storage yard
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst doing the Site Scaffold Inspections in our Kaefer Scaffold Yard today, Sunday the 7th of March, 2 x Doosan Operatives casually walked through our, barriered and controlled area.
When I approached them and asked the guys why were they were walking through our Storage Yard…. They replied that ‘they were just taking a casual walk around site and that they always go through there.’

Now, we must please remember that we treat our Fully Operational, Storage Yard on site as a working Area. The same as we would treat a barriered off, signage present, working area on site.
The Forklift is constantly moving our material around in our Storage Area and at no uncertain terms should any contractor be entering our areas without consent from Kaefer Supervision or Yardman… Mick Cape
This is for their own safety… this is the reason why there is signage on the gates. I did challenge the guys and explained the reasons why they shouldn’t be just walking through our controlled area. They took this on board and were approachable and understanding guys, however, alarm bells rang for me when they said… ‘they always go through there’

I have also had a good chat with our Yardman and advised him to report this to the Kaefer Supervision or Andy Seddon, if this continues to happen.
I have had a good chat and highlighted it to Doosan Supervision/Management on site, however this may want to be reinforced by a Uniper Representative also?

TITLE: U4 Fire Suppression CO2 Tank low level
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On 1st August 2020 CO2 in the fire suppression tank warmed and increased in pressure sufficiently to lift the pressure safety valve at 25 Bar and -12OC. On investigation the cooling compressor and fan were found not running. Various electrical and mechanical checks were performed to identify the reason for the non-running cooling system, finally a reset button on the compressor control pressure switch rectified the fault and the CO2 began to cool again. At 16:00 on the same day a subsequent check found that although the pressure and temperature had dropped to -15OC and 22 Bar, ice formed under the safety valve seat during its lifting had caused the valve to not correctly seat and loose further CO2 to a mass of 7.2 tonnes. The minimum mass required to protect the unit during operation is 8.0 tonnes so the unit was broken down until a delivery could be arranged.

TITLE: Like for like actuator issue
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Up until 2014 site had a problem in the Winter with the wellheads tripping on low temperature when the wellhead flow control valve was closed, usually when the DCS Stop or Adjustable Setpoint were reached at Pmin or Pmax. 

This trapped the gas between the wellhead and the control valve stopping the normal convection flows of warmer gas between the caverns. 

If the ambient temperature was below zero this static gas would cool to 0 degrees and activate the low temperature wellhead trip which is only intended to prevent low gas temperatures in the cavern and production tubing caused by a large, prolonged withdrawal.

To remedy this problem the trip was made ‘smart’ and was only activated if the flow control valve was open and it was deactivated when the valve was closed and no withdrawal could be occurring but this required a closed limit indication adding to the actuators. (see attached)

Since then 8 replacement actuator controllers were ordered that don’t come with the limits as standard and they have been in the stores for some time until one was fitted on H403 and were identified that the limits (there may have been an open limit fitted too) were missing.

The absence of the closed limit switch would not create a hazard and it would just generate the potential for an unnecessary trip.

This has been recorded as it is a case of a like for like replacement that isn’t.

TITLE: Lack of COVID protocols on Safety Passport training course
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
No COVID protocols were included with the joining instructions from the course provider Purple Cow Training. In answer to a request for this from me via the Engineering Academy, a COVID general information sheet v1.0 dated May 2020 was provided.

On arriving at the venue (Clock Warehouse, Derby) I enquired about the risk assessment for the training room and was told by the trainer that he did not have one, but had been assured by the provider that the room was adequate. He was expecting five delegates but there were already more than this in the room. I made a dynamic risk assessment of the room (small, low ceiling), number of people (about eight with possibly more to come, no face coverings),  their proximity (two to a desk, desk rows quite close), ventilation (small window at one end, partly opened) and duration of course (seven hours plus) and decided it was not in line with current Public Health England guidance on ventilation of indoor spaces or the current protocols for working indoors at a Uniper UK site.

TITLE: Operational loss - EDL failed
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The EDL system had gone down due to a significant network failure within the company including UGC. Being unable to enter the reduced MEL and UGC being unable to enter the MEL or reduce the PN for us, we incurred Significant Incidents from NGC for being 100Mw adrift of our PN and MEL. Eventually Siemens entered the MEL for us but not until 10:30hrs, with the EDL system down we had to receive telephone instructions for load drops to 350MW on Unit 1 and Unit 4, on EDL these will be seen as both units being 150Mw from their PN’s. As well as incurring significant incidents from NGC, there would have been significant imbalance across both unit’s and the loss of potential BOA’s or ancillary services costing us potential income.
The EDL system returned to us at 10:50 hrs when UGC informed us that their system had returned. For the record, the Nisoft system failed at the same time, this significantly impacted on us producing safety documents for the works to be carried out on the returning units, especially Unit 4 ‘A’ Coal Feeder.

TITLE: Ratcliffe Confined Space Procedures
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
I went to Ratcliffe Power Station to carry out internal visual inspection of the U3 main steam drum (part of the 2020 Statutory outage works).  This pressure vessel is classed as a “confined space”.

Prior to entry, we were informed by staff from the mechanical contractor that there was no requirement to wear any gas monitoring / detection equipment.  The mechanical contracting staff were working in the vessel when we arrived, however they exited the vessel to enable us to carry out our inspection work.

Before commencing work, we confirmed the lack of gas monitor requirement with a visit to the permit office / control room.

However, because a gas monitor is specified in our RAMS, we sourced a gas monitor from the Station Chemist and conducted our work as usual with a gas monitor attached.

This appeared to be an apparent change to the sites procedures.  Personal gas monitoring / detection equipment has been considered mandatory in confined spaces of this nature in previous years and at every other site UTG work on.   

We believe the Station has conducted a full investigation, therefore this is more for UTG learning.

The visitor returned to site about 30 minutes later with a visitor pass in a calmer manner and apologised for the incident.

TITLE: Glycol Regeneration Unit 30 Low Pressure Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Glycol Regeneration Unit 30 (GRU) tripped on Low Low Reboiler pressure when starting to process Rich Glycol. It appears QCA30AA101 Regen / Boil Off Gas Control Valve over shot when trying to balance the Reboiler pressure. On further investigation this follows similar trips on the 6th and 8th February.

This occurs as the Rich Triethylene Glycol (TEG) feed flow is increasing to close to the normal rate of around 6 m3/h. 

There is a spike in the reboiler pressure and in response the boil-off gas pressure control valve QCA30AA101 rapidly opens. This effectively controls the pressure rise which then rapidly reduces as the reboiler is vented through to the combustion chamber.

It would then appear that when a trips occurs QCA30AA101 cannot close quickly enough to maintain the reboiler pressure above the QCA30ZP005 low trip setpoint.

This trend pattern is common to all start ups but usually the pressure reduction is halted at around 30 mbarg. 

Worst case this could lead to air ingress into the reboiler from the combustion chamber creating a potentially flammable atmosphere.

However it was found that the drain valves identified on the document did not have any KKS labels fitted. These valves were 10GCN11AA401 & 402, 10GCN12AA401 & 402 and 10GCN10AA402 & 403.
The associated valves were left open but drained directly to an open bund so were not deemed as a point of isolation.
However as these valves had been quoted on the safety document the `Preparing` SAP had a responsibilities under safety rule A8 to make sure the identification of plant was adequate throughout the course of the work.

TITLE: Operational loss - U2 MBFPT Overspeed test
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst carrying out the MBFPT overspeed bolt injection the MBFP tripped causing a loss of 170MW. Tripped at 20:37 unit MEL to 330 MW from 20:53 to 21:10. The correct operational procedure was followed, with the trip bypass securely held down the manual trip was tested followed by No.1 bolt injection. Whilst selecting No.2 bolt and resetting the trip plunger the trip occurred. 

The cause is unknown, suspect an issue in the overspeed head that reduced the oil pressure which tripped the ESV and Governor valves. A successful retest was carried out when the unit dropped load before desynchronising. When discussing this with colleagues it appears the same issue has happened previously with a successful retest on that occasion

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

the WBH Bypass TCV9031 was open on startup,( SP 7degC, PV >8degC, OP 100%) But ( due to Slow acting, positioner Faulty) it did not close quickly enough resulting in COLD gas bypassing the WBH (TE9038 = 6 DegC ) 
Due to KIPS pipeline Supply pressure being at 59 Bar, a pressure drop of 40 Bar was required to supply the Power Station at 18.5 Bar ,(potential of 20 degC temperature Drop)
This resulted in -12 degC being observed at TSL9031 ESD 2oo3Trip (set -10 degC) Thus causing XV9032 to Close.

TITLE: U7 Feedwater tank high level on load causing dump valve to open to inadequate drain system
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 07 was loading up from 183MW to 410 MW following a cold start. At 11:03 a FWT Level MAX2 was received causing the emergency drain to open. Condensate control valve had opened from 50% to 69% during loading up period (to be expected) but did not close in upon receipt of high level, or when dump valve opened, therefore continued to feed the condenser at the same rate. Dump valve also had to be closed manually by the operator. Turbine hall has a lot of water deposited on to the floor as the current drain system cannot cope with this volume of water.
HP drum level feed was increasing, IP was steady and LP drum feed was decreasing.
Please could you investigate the logic, and if the dump closes on clearance of a drop in level (if at all) and if the control valve should react better to a high FW tank level.  This is becoming a more frequent occurrence on all the units.

TITLE: Lack of progress with IT connections that has now created a significant operational risk associated with the HE project at Enfield

• HE Project Team engaged IT last year on the scope and delivery requirements.
• The original agreed completion date for all IT works was w/c 23 March.
• The project team were informed on the day the IT project should have been delivered that it is now 2 months late (potentially 3 to full completion)
•  An order for a dedicated 100mb BT broadband line with a 60d ay lead time had not been processed.
•  IT were engaging a 3 person family contract business
• The late delivery leaves operations with a contract claims risk. 
• The operations team is now having to organise elements on the installation to get things moving.

Field core operating procedures were followed and the tool was secured in place to stop any items falling.

Additional information, I was in the process of concluding a short (~2 min) hands free call with my Son, when the collision occurred.

TITLE: Displacement of load whilst lifting with overhead crane
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A rotor had to be lifted off a lorry trailer for storage in the PES workshop. The rotor was already attached to the customer built lifting cradle. A drawing supplied by the customer highlighted the total weight, CoG and the lifting points. A local lifting plan was produced in line with PES procedure. The plan was to lift the load clear of the trailer, remove the trailer and lower the load 1.5mts to the ground. This procedure was adhered to but whilst lowering the load, it suddenly shifted forward slightly, causing the CoG to move thus resulting in an unbalanced load. TITLE: High pressure at pressure reduction valve manifold
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During an injection nomination at around 00:00, high pressure seen at pressure reduction valve (PRV) manifold (cavern pressure). On investigation no differential pressure was seen across the equalisation valve to the heat exchangers. Technician went to investigate and the equalisation gas bypass valve was open, despite showing closed on the plant control system (DCS). The valve was isolated at the time and then subsequently the limits were reset, during investigation at the time it appears to have lost it limits. Difficult to determine exactly why the limits were not correct as this occurred during the middle of the night. 

Believed a contributing factor could have been that the inlet separator valves may also have been passing and an increased pressure was observed at Inlet Separator 20 by the operator.

If the pressure had carried on increasing the plant would have tripped on high pressure.

TITLE: Emergency Stop button activated on 5t overhead crane following the "up  control" button becoming stuck.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The task was to lower the 15mts fabric slings into a storage crate after lifting the generator rotor onto a flatbed lorry. The 5t hoist was selected for this task. The slings were to be lifted so they are fully extended and then lowered into the crate. Whilst extending the slings, the banksman signalled a stop sign to the crane operator after noticing the close proximity of a sling to the cantilever scaffolding. The crane driver immediately reacted and depressed the up button but unfortunately the hoist didn't stop and the hook continued to rise. Almost immediately, the sling caught a scaffold pole and the operator reacted by hitting the emergency stop button. After a quick assessment, the crane was repositioned and the slings lowered into the storage box.
No other working party was in the vicinity during the activity.

TITLE: Deluge system remained isolated following test.

CNC-02-JPH-HV -076 is the discharge isolation valve for Zone 5 which provides water deluge fire protection for Bearings 4, 5, 6 & 7.
The fire valves had been checked in the corrected position during the previous months routine carried out on 10/12/2018.

A LWC for the Activation of Deluge & Visual checks had been issued to TYCO on 17/12/18.
The work carried out under this LWC allowed for the operation of the above valve.
It is a possibility that the CNC-02-JPH-HV -076 was inadvertently left in the closed position following the deluge test.

TITLE: Review of alarm arrangements in compressors
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A HGSL Operator is developing a simulator of the control system.  This work requires systematic review of the alarm arrangements across the installation.  When reviewing smoke and gas detection within the compressor enclosures, the Operator noticed that the code for the compressor to "fail safe" in the event of detector power-loss did not reflect the arrangement elsewhere on the site.  Hence, based on the operators concern that the detectors were not "fail safe", testing was undertaken on the same day to isolate the power and review the function of the code.  The test identified that the detectors were fail safe, but used a slightly different code - most likely due to the automatic EDP function found on the compressors but not elsewhere on the plant.

This report has been raised to document both the findings of the test and to note the potential benefit in such proactive alarm reviews.

TITLE: BWSC Brigg Renewable Energy Plant
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a practice evacuation, two contract staff were working inside the boiler and when the alarm was raised were unable to here it. the hole watcher tried to contact them but when unsuccessful reported to the muster point and informed the station staff of the situation.
I also reported the missing staff following a role call to station staff.
The evacuation practice was terminated and the rescue team went to the location to investigate the reason for the missing staff, finding that they could not hear, station is looking into improving communications i.e.
Air horns for the hole watchers 
I have said that although part of one working party if people are working separately they are to have radio communication.
Station have also been looking into a tag in system, although this would not have improved the situation.

TITLE: Exposed hot pipework after insulation removal
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
As part of an ongoing programme of work to check for corrosion under insulation (CUI) on pipework the insulation had been removed from the Triethylene Glycol (TEG) Booster Pump delivery lines to inspect the pipework on Glycol Regeneration Unit 20 (GRU 20).

This work had been done when the unit was offline, when the unit was bought back online this left exposed potentially hot surfaces (~200 degrees when the unit is on line) without any barriers being erected to restrict access. 

In addition, protective film had been applied to provide weather protection but this was melting on to the pipe. 

GRU 30 had also had some insulation removed on a Booster Pump delivery line and the protective film had also melted on to the exposed pipework.

TITLE: IP CV North loss of control
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
02:15 Plant loading up from 3356MW BOA to 410MW PN
02:50 Prior to the event there was a rise in 18MAD20CY022 to 172um (which also happened on Sunday when there was a similar IP CV issue). This dropped right off once the plant load was stable
02:50 ST sequencer alarms received.
02:57 IP CV north started to open and close erratically.
Local observations were unable to prove that the valve was physically moving, however:
the IP drum level started to rise, 
the LP system pressure increased to alarm value, 
the plant load had become unstable,  
the IP CV south started to move in response to the IP CV norths position,
18MAB10CP001 pressure of steam IP inlet was unstable,
LP by-pass opening and LP drum level falling,
The Vickers card panel was displaying a intermittent flashing red light,
Decided to drop load to 230MW to stabilise the plant and avoid possible trip.

03:26 Called Trading to REMIT MEL down to 230MW until 06:00
03:29 Called CH
03:48 Plant at 230MW and stable - Both IP CV's open at 100% and IP and LP by-passes closed.
03:56 Called Trading to REMIT MEL to 230MW until 12:00.

TITLE: Operational loss (not process safety) - U1 Boiler recirc pump tripped / came out of service
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U1 Boiler Recirc pump tripped/came out of service on Sat 07/03 @ 08:20 hrs with no abnormal alarms received, we were unable to restart the pump because when the pump was found out of service on a panel check, we were just outside of the 2.5hr window where we allowed restart it.
We have done some preliminary investigations and it appears the pump shut down around the time we were carrying out our routine weekend checks.
The particular checks in question involve us pressing the A & B side drum hydrastep level check alarm test buttons that are located on the Unit ESD panel, to confirm the alarm works.
We have carried out a controlled test and it appears that if both A & B side hydrasteps level buttons are tested at the same time, or in quick succession (both alarms up at the same time) this then takes the pump out of service on a drum low level (drum level low should trip the pump under normal conditions), however if the hydrasteps are tested one at a time then the pump remains in service. No alarms are received to indicate the recirc pump has tripped.

TITLE: Acid leak in acid bund
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a routine water treatment plant stream regeneration it was found that acid had leaked from the system into the acid bund. The process was immediately stopped, and isolation valves closed. The acid within the bund was fuming off at this point making it difficult to approach the area, but estimations of level was about 3-4mm. Personnel withdraw from the area and opened exterior doors to provide some ventilation.
Email sent to all members of staff advising of the situation and asking them to cascade this to their direct reports and contractors.
After some discussion on the way forward and a Dynamic risk assessment had been carried out, an Operation Technician donned suitable PPE and respirator and re-entered the WTP room and pumped out the bund into the main sump. The bund was then washed down and pumped into the main sump, ready to be sent to the neutralisation tank.
The cause of the leak is suspected to be vent from the double block and bleed valve. There was no evidence of wet on the motor support plate or surrounding pipework.
