TITLE: Unit late Sync.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit operations staff were unaware that the there had been a PN entered for CDC to Sync to the Grid at 16.00. Operations team had been told that the Unit was standing in the BM all day and had not had any communication with the Uniper trading team. There was also no display to indicate the sync time on the GPMS screen.
Whilst carrying out other duties the operations team noticed that the GPMS display was displaying a sync time. Contact was immediately made with the Uniper trading team who confirmed that the PN was indeed correct. They also stated that the PN had been entered the previous day. 
Trading team informed of the error and told that the unit would be one hour late. The unit eventually synced to the Grid at 16.55 (55 minutes) late. 
After several attempts the operations team managed to reboot the GPMS browser and the problems were reported to the Siemens team.
Reference number 13205280 obtained and emails sent to the relevant parties. Neil Griffin form Siemens contacted site later and discussed the issues. However he was unable to dial in so will investigate further when connection obtained.

TITLE: Operational Loss - Ammonia fogging system
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 02:39hrs on 24/8 the Ammonia Fogging system initiated with a number of alarms associated with Ammonia Tank B, including Toxic Gas Alarm.
With Breathing apparatus we carefully inspected the Ammonia compound and Tank B, it was soon apparent that there was no actual gas leakage and when inspecting the Sensors the following was noted:

Q138 B Tank, Gas Detector B – digital readout stated ‘Sensor Missing’,
Q137 B Tank, Gas Detector A – digital readout stated ‘Alarm Fault’.

The Fogging Deluge system reinitiated after 20 minutes, then repeated every 5 to 10 mins, setting the Mulsifyre Pump off at a time when the pump was set to its alternative supply.

TITLE: Smouldering detected (Adicos Alarm) in both Woodpellet Silo's due to sensitive settings of Adicos (and reactive Woodpellets).
CASE_DESCRIPTION: CoCom is currently being commissioned (co-firing of woodpellets into MPP3). Planned for project handover from 1st of January 2020. On 29th of November due to Adicos alarm (smouldering detection) there was a switch over to coal. After investigation it was concluded that batch of pellets (Ricarda) must have been more reactive than earlier batches, which triggered the sensitive settings of Adicos. The Adicos detection limits were set from ‘open air mode’ (which makes the settings more sensitive). They are now correctly set by Adicos to ‘silo’ setting (robust, since its a silo). Inerting with N2 of silo set until fully emptied. 2/12 Inspection of (empty) Silo to ensure no smouldering wood pellets were left behind.

TITLE: Operational Loss (not process safety)- CW system
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst dosing the CW system with Hypochlorite on the day shift 11/09/19 W1 Residual Chlorine monitor went into alarm reading approximately 0.3ppm. Checked by Chemist manual sample to be no greater than 0.1ppm. 
Upon immediate investigation it was found that the flow to the cell of the instrument had been interrupted by "slime" but the constant head device was still flowing so there wasn't and alarm indicting loss of flow. 
On the night shift 11/09/19 when dosing again the same situation occurred and again dosing was stopped as soon as the alarm
initiated and the purge flow adjusted accordingly. 
The C & I team investigated as soon as they arrived on the following day shift to confirm that the cell had blocked again. Although this was not a breach of our permit there are still implications and reporting required.

TITLE: Operational loss - U3 high extraction pump conductivities
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 24/10 U3 was fired and steam to set occurred, it was showing high extraction pump conductivities >5uS before and after column. on the return to service unit 3 boiler chemistry deviated from target conditions. The extraction pump chemistry went into alarm state 3 (>1.0uS after column conductivity) during its on load run and the boiler water chemistry followed with the after column conductivity peaking at 51uS (alarm state 3). 
Due to the unit being ran to increase pressure for trevi testing there was no caustic dosing in the boiler water therefore no
boiler water protection. The pH of the feed flow and boiler water remained beneath the required level for the duration. LP dosing only occurred whilst the unit was generating. 
The boiler was dosed on the morning of 26/10 with a firing dose after discussions with a boiler team representative and the trevi continued after the dose had been added. The boiler was fired for 3hours after the trevi test was completed to facilitate blowdown and dosing of the boiler water. There was no steam sample available to assess the amount of sodium that has passed through the attemperator sprays into the superheaters. Both shells of the condenser had saw dust added to try and slow the ingress of contaminants and it was questioned if a condenser shell could be taken out of service to help to identify which shell the leak was in.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
CDC module was at full load.
A large flame was witnessed on the control room CCTV coming from the west side of the top of the gas turbine.
A decision was made to manually trip the gas turbine from the control room  back panel emergency stop push button as simultaneously the fire alarm panel began to sound.
The above all proceeded within approximately 30 seconds of the flames being witnessed.
The site evacuation alarm was sounded along with a tannoy instruction to evacuate site.
The station MEL was redec'd to 0MW and remitted with energy trading.
The plant was observed as it was shutdown and the visible flames stopped on the tripping of the plant.  
The main gas valve 10EKG70AA001 was closed and gas vented to remove all gas from the building. The FGPH outlet valves were manually closed to 10EFG70AA001 passing.
Approximately 15 minutes after the GT being tripped a visual inspection was made of the GT which confirmed the dislodging of a flange thought to be that of the flame eye and lagging being emitted from the blow off pipework on the west side of the GT.
As there was no further risk to personnel the site evacuation was ended with the UMC remaining off limits and locked down.
Further inspection and repair planning commenced with the Engineering Team.

TITLE: Fuel Gas Pre-Heater shutdown / tripped causing GT Humming.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Valve 10EKT25AA101 FG P/HTR CIRC CTRL-V faulted with ‘Trouble Alarm’ and ‘Status Discrepancy Not Closed’. The valve had to be put in local operation at the Fuel Gas Pre-heater location and then manually operated in the open and closed  directions, the ‘fault re-set’ was then operated to clear the fault.  Multiple notifications under 21347109 are available to view valve fault history.  
During the valve fault the flow rate on the heating water side dropped and shut down the fuel gas preheater program.
 When the fuel gas preheater shuts down cooler natural gas flows to the GT burners. During this transition from Hot Gas to cooler gas the Gas turbine suffers combustion instability and combustion chamber rumble occurs causing GT Humming protection systems to operate.  
On the morning of 29-03-2021 the GT Humming protection operated as a direct result of cooler natural gas temperatures causing 0.2s to be added to the humming counter, there was a slight drop in load as the GT setpoint controller was switched off causing a slight imbalance during a load transient.

TITLE:
Gasoliespill naar terrein en haven
Spill of gasoil to site area and harbour
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Tijdens de start van MPP3 is er gasolie terecht gekomen in het stoomsysteem. Uiteindelijk is deze gasolie via de ontspantank in waterdamp/gasolie-vorm over het Uniper-terrein verspreid met de windrichting mee. Tevens is er een kleine fractie gasoliehoudend water via het LCL-systeem richting spuivijver verpompt.

During start-up of MPP3, 2 integrated drain valves of the steam atomizing system and the gasoil system of 1 burner were in the wrong (open) position. The drain route to the leakage tank was blocked-in causing the gasoil (25 bar) to penetrate the steam atomizing system (10 bar). The gasoil entered the (steam condensate) drain water expansion vessel which is atmospheric in pressure due to an open pipeline to the roof of the boiler house. Via the roof (+125 m) and high winds (43 km/hr), the mixture of water vapor and gasoil spilled over the location during a period of 3 to 4 hrs. Simultaneously a fraction of the same mixture of condensate and gasoil from the drain water expansion vessel was pumped into the main cooling water outlet basin discharging to surface water.

TITLE: Potential for Duplicate Swipe Card Numbers to be allocated with different Access Control Cards
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Recently at Ratcliffe we've taken delivery of 600 new HID access control cards.  As of last month our previously issued E.On access control cards ran out and we started issuing from the new batch.

After a few days a couple of users informed us that when setting up SecurePrint on their new cards, when scanning in on the printers instead of taking them through the registration process it logged them in as another user.

We believe that this is due to the stored numbers on the two active people's different cards being the same, and/or SecurePrint not using the site code portion of the access control cards.

This is a data protection risk as there is a chance that these users with duplicate card numbers could print sensitieve personal data off the SecurePrint queue from that account that they are incorrectly logged into.

I've attached a flow diagram to explain the problem.

Fundamentally we believe that the fragmented way that Access Control cards are issued across the company and having a company wide access control card swipe system for the printers is why the risk of duplicate numbers on Access control cards is a data protection risk.

There is also a potential that these duplicate cards could allow someone access to another site that they are not authorised, but we don't believe this risk is high as the access control systems should use the site codes as well, but this will need investigating.

TITLE: Testing of HV cables associated with SC10 SFC
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The tests were conducted by ICS who had installed, glanded & terminated the cables on behalf of EMI.

The agreed test was a VLF test for 15 minutes at 19kV RMS (27kV peak) on three conductors simultaneously.

People present:-

Uniper – Dave Rowlands (SFT)
Siemens – Louis Bucholsky
ICS – Graham Sloan (Test Engineer)
ICS – John More

Sequence of events:-

•	C/O Panel – Fuse Panel & C/O Panel – SFC Panel cables tested successfully
•	SFC Transformer - SFC Panel (10CJN91) cables (9 off) confirmed disconnected both ends
•	Continuity test of all 9 cables completed
•	Transformer cable ends all well clear 
•	U1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and insulated boots positioned between cable lugs and busbar
•	V1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and to earth and booted
•	W1 cable ends (3 off) in SFC panel connected together and to earth
•	1kV DC insulation resistance test conducted successfully on U1 cables 
•	19kV VLF test started on U1 cables
•	Flashover was heard 2 maybe 3 times in quick succession before the test was terminated. It is assumed the flashover occurred between one of the U1 cable ends and the U1 busbar.

TITLE: U1 OUTAGE - FLT Transporting Generator Casing Steel Plate
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A near hit incident occurred involving a forklift and a stack of heavy steel plates. The incident took place at outside Unit 1 turbine hall at approximately 14:05

Details of the Incident:

Forklift Operator:  PES 
Equipment Involved, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates.
As the forklift took a corner, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:
The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
The area was cordoned off to ensure safety until the situation was stabilized.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:
Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.

TITLE: Oil store flooding due to Mulsifyre system discharge
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the electrical works conducted on weekend of 15th/16th Feb the supplies to the oil store were isolated.  The mulsifyre system was still live and the loss of supplies to the store included loss to the mulsifyre compressor which primes the air sensing lines.  When the pressure in the lines dropped the fire system was discharged in the oil storage area.  This deluge caused damage to several boxes of grease cartridges and also allowed oil drip trays to overflow.  The contents of which went down the station drains.

Oily water also proceeded to pass through to the office area and into the switchroom and down a cable tunnel.

This was not discovered properly until Tuesday 18th Feb as the Altrad oil supervisor was working in the main stores on Monday 17th Feb and didn't go in to the oil stores.  Legacy issues with the fire alarm system prevented the Operation teams from identifying where the mulsifyre system had been discharged and led them to believe there was a significant leak.

TITLE: PSO - Main Control Block Fire Alarm

The area identified was zone 1 ground floor. A burning smell was evident on entry to the area. When opening the Inverter Room switchroom door thick smoke and burning smell was evident. The switchroom was ventilated and checks of adjacent areas of the switchroom annex confirmed that the source of the smoke was from the Inverter Room. As the smoke cleared, on inspection none of the equipment in the associated switchroom appeared to be in distress! With the support of the electrical team each panel was inspected and it was believed that EML4 lighting inverter was the most likely source although it was still operating apparently normally.

TITLE: Humber Oil Refinery (P66) Condensate Valve ESD Trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The pressure of the steam to the Uniper heat exchanger rose to 4 bar and this caused the condensate ESD valve trip to shutting off the return line to HOR. HOR provide the steam for this system.
The system is designed to protect the steam pipework from gas infiltration caused by a tube break in the heat exchanger. However due to system design the pressure monitoring is on the steam side of the heat exchanger and is set at 4 bar, the system normally runs at approx 3 .5 bar.
The issue would be cold gas to the refinery which should be supplied at above 0 Deg C  ,with the valve shutoff the gas temperature remained above that.

TITLE: Failure of level transmitter during test
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During routine testing of the liquid level still chamber.
The “Control” level transmitter was found to have values entered the upper and lower ranges, that were different to the identical safety transmitter and identical control level transmitters on the two other identical vessels. 

It was also observed that the amplitude of the waveform seemed to be significantly lower than on the same device at other positions. 

The still well was filled with water and the level increase – immediately an issue with the “0” position was obvious the water level continued to be increased and no response was given from the transmitter.

The correct parameters were entered, and the waveform threshold retuned. 
The liquid level test then recommenced. 
The transmitter performed as expected at 
0 ,25,50,75,100% points. 

As the still well drained, the Transmitter registered the 75% point, however after that the reading froze despite the still chamber being totally empty. 

Should this have happened in normal operation the control valve could have opened despite the liquid level not being present. 

This would have likely put a demand on the SIF responsible for this protection.

We quickly made an assessment of the fire and the resources to hand

Further observations were such that the source of heat was associated with the brindle dry wood used to store the spare Titanium Condenser Tubes and 
the heat radiated from the metal work. There was no evidence of cigarette ends and or other third party source of ignition."

TITLE: Sync Comp 400kV Alarms
CASE_DESCRIPTION: At 00:11 on 28/7/24 we received a 400kV interposing relay 110V DC MCB Trip alarm. This was raised as a P1 notification and communicated via email, although it did not cause any issues with the sync comp but it was a worrying alarm when added to other alarms that had been standing. A further alarm, 400kV CP 1 relay inoperative initiated at 11:15 and at 12:26 all indication was lost on X490, X493A, X493B & X493C, this prompted a discussion with TNCC and a request was made for the on call NGET SAP to attend site. On arrival, as expected from a previous alarm, the 110v battery charger was in fault and the output volts had dropped to 50V DC. This was the reason for the faults and it transpired, we had lost the fast acting trip capability.

TITLE: Minor smoldering fire in grid operator equipment at power plant Pfrombach
CASE_DESCRIPTION: On Sunday 2nd of May a minor smouldering fire occurred in the power plant Pfrombach at river Isar. The fire was related to an external equipment (switchgear)operated by the Bayernwerk grid operator and stopped without any counter measures and/or firefighters. The external equipment is located within the building operated by Hydro and therefore the alarm from the installed automatic fire detection systems (smoke) was detected by our central control room. Stand by duty was sent to the side to manage the situation. On site they met the stand by duty from Bayernwerk who also detected the failure and fixed the equipment to continue operation as planned. No Uniper equipment was damaged.

TITLE: Maintenance Order discrepancy between operational line description and PRT.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: I was looking to assess a Maintenance Order for set up actuator unit 4 FSR-UV -051. The operational line is for setting up the actuator and the long text stated set up actuator and adjust limits and torque settings. There is no safe system of work in the long text so i had a look at the PRT which is for generic Kaefer actuator stroke check fault find which allows them to carry out a full range of jobs including IR and balance checks,replacement of components and boards etc. If I had assessed this job on the long text the competent person would have had a Safety Document that i thought was for stroke checking the actuator but the method of work allows them to possibly do much more work. In my opinion there should be something written in to GMI SHE 003 which makes it clear that the work scope and method of work that an SAP assesses for the job from the long text needs to match any PRT.

TITLE: Nearmiss During AHM
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
I am writing to report a nearmiss incident that I witnessed during the boat deployment to the water. 
A person who was stepping off the boat towards the porch almost got her foot struck by the strut of the boat and the rock on the shore side. The boat was moving closer to the shore and the clearance was very narrow. 
The person was unaware of the potential hazard and managed to avoid it by stepping on the rock quickly.

TITLE: Forklift Truck Transporting Generator Steel Casing Plates
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Forklift Operator: PES

Equipment Involved: Forklift, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates from the turbine hall on U1.
As the forklift took a corner whilst reversing backwards, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:

The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:

Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.

TITLE: U4 Upsurge Control Valve No515 Control Air Valve missing isolation lock
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The safety isolation key for the Upsurge Control Valve No.515 Control Air valve was released from the T3B cascade key safe following the return of the T3B PFW.  The release of this key (safety key No 9727) allowed us to prepare for the PFW ROMP (Permit For Work with Restoration Of Motive Power), for the re-connection of the valve 515 and setting of the valve limits.   Following release of the key on the morning of the 13/07, the Outage Commissioning operative was asked to attach a ROMP notice to the valve in preparation for the issue of the safety document.  On getting to the valve location it was noted that there was no isolation lock on the valve as expected.  The chain that was used to isolate the valve was still attached to the valve body / pipework but there was no sign of the isolation lock.
The control valve and actuator had both been removed & replaced during the Outage period.  The air pipework and the valve spindle had both been disconnected to allow the removal / replacement of the valve / actuator.  The air isolation valve was not directly local to the valve, it was the master isolator approx 6ft away on the adjacent wall.
The Authorised Persons Isolation sheet was checked, and the isolation point had been double checked and double signed for at the start of the Outage period when the T3B cascade box was established; on release of the safety key from the key safe the signatures were crossed off of the AP sheet.  The immediate area was searched for any sign of a broken / damaged lock, but nothing could be found.

TITLE: Misuse of 'Man Down' feature on Site Radios
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the evening of 16th July 2024 around 20:00, the night security guard set off the ‘Man Down’ alert on his site radio, which was subsequently reset. Later, whilst undertaking the 22:00 site tour, the security guard failed to take the Gatehouse radio & site security mobile phone.
The Gatehouse radio was left in the Gatehouse and set to ‘Man Down On’ and thus activated an alert on the Gatehouse, CDC & KPS Control Room radio base stations.
Operations personnel in the CDC Control Room attempted to contact the security guard on the radio & site security mobile phone, to no avail.
Fortunately, operations personnel in the CDC Control Room were able to spot the security guard walking around site, which negated the need to escalate the matter. Operations personnel in the CDC Control Room were able to speak to the security guard on his return to the Gatehouse and instigated additional contact protocols to ensure there were no repeat occurrences that night.
The following morning, upon his arrival to site, the day security guard reset the Gatehouse radio base station which was still in alarm. The night security guard simply turned off the Gatehouse radio and turned down the volume on the Gatehouse radio base station to silence the audible alert, as he did not know how to reset it.

On the evening of 22nd July 2024, the same security guard once again set off the ‘Man Down’ radio alert and was given instruction on how to reset it by Killingholme operations personnel. However, at the start of the morning shift on 23rd July 2024, Killingholme operations personnel found the KPS Control Room radio base station in alert, so it would appear the security guard had triggered the alert again at some point during the night.

These are serious matters of concern, which highlight the security guard’s lack of understanding and discipline, repeatedly creating unnecessary work for numerous Uniper personnel.

TITLE: Poor electrical installation
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During commissioning work for the Ambient Air Injection project, the drawings supplied by Schneider for the two new HMC1172 6.6kV VCB control panels were found to be roughly 75% accurate. There was also a suspicion that the motor heaters were remaining live, despite the fuses being pulled from the circuit. Work was put together, to validate the drawings and produce an as built drawing. During this work, it was found that the outgoing heater connections for both the new 6.6kV motors had been linked together, and then fed from the next closest HMC panel with motor heater connections. This meant that, if any of the three panels heater fuses were in place, all three motor heater circuits would be live.

TITLE: Loose scaffold boards resulting in small gap in platform
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst working on a scaffold platform on SC20 during the KH outage for disconnection and reconnection of the flexible busbar links, a contractor was transporting a bucket containing nuts, bolts, and washers when two of the scaffold boards on the platform slipped, resulting in a small gap opening up approximately 4-5 inches at its widest point. The contractor's leg slipped through the gap approximately up to the knee joint. The contractor was wearing a removable knee pad which caught on the scaffold boards preventing the leg from dropping any further. No injuries were sustained during the incident, however several nuts and washers were ejected from the bucket during the fall and dropped approximately 10 feet to the next level below. On closer inspection, it appears that the two scaffold boards that slipped were not sufficiently clipped in place, allowing them to slide under the weight of the contractor.

TITLE: Near hit in car
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Monday 16th  on my way to work i was involved in a near accident, I say near because although i came very close to hitting another car I believe there was no contact. The incident occurred on a roundabout when the driver in from pulled forward onto the roundabout then immediately stopped. I was pulling forward into the space the car had left, I was travelling at less than 5mph. I braked but did not feel any contact with the car in front. Both the driver and I pulled over to the side of the road to look at any damage. On the other drivers car there was no obvious sign of damage or even a scuff mark . The other driver did point out a small crack but this looked like old damage as it had road grime in it and appeared to have a small puncture mark.  I did not claim responsibility and said that I was not responsible for that as it was old. There was no sign of any mark on my car at all not even the road dirt had been effected. We exchange details as required to do so. The other driver has now contacted me  claiming I caused that damage. I told the driver that I was not responsible for the damage but they have since contacted me again asking for either payment to get the repair done or my insurance details. I have provided my insurance details.  Other driver white Mini Registration YK18 YOX. Notified to Uniper Fleet and Travel and Lex as possible claim (fraudulent?)

TITLE: Furnace Trip due to Naphtha KOD tank overfilled.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
First Incident:  4/12/2021
CPU 1 was undergoing start up after SW 30 shutdown. Almost at the end of start-up activity the following happened:
1.	At 0110hrs received Furnace Non Urgent Alarm in DCS.
2.	On checking at furnace BMS panel by operator, found Naphtha KOD level was around 10% and continuously dropping, but instead of appearing LAL-1711 and LALL-1711, the displayed alarm was LAH-1711 and LAHH-1711.
3.	Furnace firing was stopped immediately from DCS and Field Operator (FO) was rushed to field to check for any leak.
4.	Checked physically at site and found the naphtha KOD was full.
Action Taken
1.	Vessel drained and reduced the level to reset LAH-1711 and LAHH-1711
2.	Drained LIT-1711 and LIT-1713 LP and HP impulse lines
3.	Reset the alarm in BMS panel and restarted the furnace
4.	Observed the KOD vessel level control cut-in and cut-off working well.
Second Incident: 4/12/2021
1.	At 1615 hrs Non urgent alarm appeared on SCADA.
2.	1615 hrs checked in Furnace PLC for alarm details, it was showing LAL-1711 (13 %) and continued going down trend.
3.	At that point of time Naphtha flow to furnace was 1.2 TPH and P-004 to KOD was 1.9 TPH (KOD  level control XV open and close function was ok throughout shift).
4.	KOD level continue decreasing, informed FO to increased flow to KOD to prevent furnace Naphtha pump tripping on LAL-1711. (16:19 to 16:21 hrs).
5.	At 1621 hrs LALL-1711 appear  in PLC and furnace Naphtha pump got tripped on LL but furnace not tripped and continue firing with 250Kg/hr flow rate.
6.	Furnace temperature continued to go down, so unit kept on long circulation at 1630 hrs and later kept on short circulation.
7.	Informed FO to check KOD physically, FO found KOD was over filled.
8.	Stop Naphtha feeding to KOD by closing XV-322.
9.	KOD emptied out.
Similar third and fourth incident happened on 6/12/2021 at 0145 hrs and on 14/12/2021 at 1152 hrs respectively

TITLE: Paint spillage Tech Centre
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Paint was being removed from the COSHH cabinet in the Integral engineer area in the rig bay roof, to be relocated to the COSHH cabinet in the shed. 

We had made the decision to do this, following the issuance of the FRA and comments made concerning the rig bay roof. 

Office Essentials loaded the paints onto a rolling cage and took them to the goods lift, where they were moved to the ground floor and out of the external door into the carpark. 

As they moved the cage down the slope into the car park, the door came undone and a tin of paint fell onto the floor, the lid came off and a small amount of emulsion paint spilled onto the tarmac surface. 

This was highlighted to David Gray and Cassie Hall who cleaned up the spill with absorbent pads and blue roll from the spill kit. 

There was a thin residue left on the floor that could not be wiped up further with pads / wipes. 

David Gray decided to wash down the area with water to dilute what was left of the paint, after no more could be removed by the absorbent pads.

TITLE: Gas leak from faulty isolation valve
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst carrying our flushing and greasing activities on Inlet Separator 10 inlet valve, there was an unexpected gas leak due to a faulty isolation valve. 

The capped screw has a drilled tell-tail to allow for any pressure behind to vent before the cap can be fully removed to prevent any potential injury due to build up of pressure.

As the cap was unscrewed, the pressure was released from the tell-tail and instead of it being a short sharp hiss, it was continuous indicating the fitting had failed.  It has a non-return valve and a ball valve but on this occasion both were passing. The same isolation valve was used yesterday with no issues.

This has shown as large amounts of positive imbalance on our systems.

TITLE: U7 B Inspection Commissioning Delay
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U7 B Inspection commissioning was delayed due to quality and safety issues:


•	Access. Due to the reintroduction of the full LP OTC PEM120, the new ST PEM120 area and the proliferation of scaffolding still present, it has been a challenge getting around the Plant and Equipment.

•	During filling of the HRSG & Drums it was noted that with both HP FRV closed, the HP Drum continued to fill at approximately 16kg/s. This will cause issues during start-up and shutdown.

•	IP Drum Intermittent Blowdown actuator indicating 6000%. Actuator operates locally.

•	LP Drum Intermittent Blowdown actuator is in fault and not operating from the DCS. Actuator operates locally.

•	Stack Damper does not operate or indicate from the DCS. Opened locally and OPEN/CLOSE signals pinned at the DCS when required.

•	SAM Fan No.1 de-isolated but tripped on start and now shows a Starter Fault that will not reset.

•	LP OTC Level Tx 2 requires the impulse line pumping up. – Start Inhibit.

•	IP Bypass Spray Water CV is not indicating closed and requires a CLOSE Pin to allow the FG to shut down successfully.

•	HP SH Drain / DSH Drain valves 71HAH52AA204 & 202 are isolated and on PFW 2025/00925 to “Reroute cables and reconnect actuators to valves”

•	Manway door by LP Int Blowdown Actuator does not look like it has been fitted properly and most of the nuts are hand tight or missing.

TITLE: Incorrect storage and segregation of waste
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
After a routine waste inspection around site it was identified that the general, dry mixed recycling and WEEE waste bins located in the workshop were full and overflowing. The general waste bin contained non-conforming waste. 

The general and DMR bins have scheduled kerbside collections weekly. As the bins were moved inside without notification these collections have been missed. Additionally, due to the non-conforming waste it is fortunate that these have been missed otherwise we would have been charged additional fees and potentially reported for failing to segregate hazardous and non-hazardous waste.

TITLE: PEM120 - GRA-61-MBM-10 - U6 EV COMBUSTOR
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the U61 A07 Inspection the EV LHS split line insulation was found internally damaged during removal. This was first evidence of hot air leakage in this area. At this time Ansaldo and UTL supported an opportunity based reinspect and monitor strategy which was implemented.

Upon visual inspection during the U61 B03 Inspection the insulation was found further deteriorated in the local area. GE were now involved and they took images and feeler gauge measurements of the area. It measures 0.05mm gap across approx. 200mm length which confirmed the leakage path.

There is currently only localised signs of heat around the area, particularly on insulation blanket directly on top of the leak area. GT enclosure temperature is currently steady. Based on this the leakage is assumed to be minor currently. But the confirmation of leakage gap and length checks has initiated this exclusion zone assessment to manage any further deterioration.

TITLE: Confined-space atmospheric hazard – CO alarm triggered; controlled evacuation of CQ U3 IP Drum
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During an internal inspection of the CQ Unit 3 HRSG IP drum  the entrants’ personal multi-gas monitor alarmed for elevated CO. 2 entrants were inside and the designated attendant (top-man) waited outside. Top-man immediately exercised stop-work authority, instructed a controlled evacuation, and managed the egress. From a safe position outside the vessel, the atmosphere was re-tested using the gas monitor on an extension probe to exclude instrument fault; readings confirmed elevated CO within the drum. The job was paused, the permit suspended, and the area isolated, with escalation to the Supervisor/HSSE.
Actual outcome: Near miss, no injury or illness.
Potential consequence: Asphyxiation/physiological effects due to CO displacement of O₂.
Immediate actions: Stop-work initiated; entrants evacuated; atmosphere verified; re-entry prohibited pending review of ventilation/purging and controls.
Preliminary factors for investigation: Effectiveness of purge/ventilation; possible CO ingress/accumulation pathway; confirmation of gas-monitor calibration and bump-test records.
Positive observation: The attendant’s prompt, calm response exemplified our Beyond Zero behaviours and prevented potential exposure.

TITLE: Aton Project - Torque Tube Unloading near miss
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The EPC's subcontractor's employees had the following task in the three parks of the Aton project. A truck arrived at the park's organizational area carrying support structure pipes for the project. No shipment assembled in this way had arrived before, so there were no written instructions in the MS on how to unload the shipment from the truck, and no training was provided. The employees of the subcontractor in consultation with the construction manager of construction lead company came up with the following solution: using three forklifts, they would lift the load at the same time, and then, after lifting, the truck would drive out from under the load. When the truck drove out, the three forklifts would move forward at the same time and place the load down in sync at the designated location. The work process was started by a controller operating the three forklifts. They lifted the load (kb. 9t), the truck drove out from under the load, they started moving forward, and when they set down the load, one of the forklifts lagged behind in lowering the load, causing the load to tilt, the forklifts jammed, and the load fell over from approximately 50cm to the ground. The fallen load hit the other load that had already been unloaded, so it had to be propped up. After the incident, the construction manager of was notified.

TITLE: Site Radios safety concern
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There are significant safety concerns regarding the new site radios currently in use at Grain.

Issue Summary:

Dead Spots: There are areas across the site where radios fail to receive or transmit messages, leading to critical communication blackouts.

Encryption Hindrance: The newly introduced encryption has notably disrupted communication flow across the site. The additional delay and complexity—especially with the double-tap function—has led to repeated miscommunications, which could prove dangerous in emergency situations.

Man Down Feature Reliability: While we’ve seen a decrease in false alarms reaching the control room, this has come at the cost of reliability. During upcoming outages, the influx of contractors unfamiliar with the equipment will likely lead to increased spurious alarms and confusion.

Incident Simulation & Findings:

During a recent test of the “man down” function:

The CCR responded to the alarm by attempting contact via the emergency channel, which should have automatically connected. However, this communication was overridden by the radio’s repeating alarm signal.

The CCR received no indication from the base station that the message had failed.

Upon failure, the CCR attempted to reset the alarm via the base station. While it appeared to reset, the alarm remained active on the radio, creating a false impression that the situation was resolved.

No follow-up response was initiated, as the incident was mistakenly assumed to be a false alarm.

Safety Concern:

This exposes a critical flaw in both the communication and alarm systems. The man down function, in its current implementation, cannot be relied upon to trigger an appropriate emergency response. Furthermore, the system provides no clear feedback loop to confirm whether a situation is genuine or resolved.

Request for Action:

We strongly recommend the following actions:

Review and audit the coverage and communication integrity of the current radio system across site.

Evaluate the effectiveness of the man down feature—consider disabling it until it can reliably support life-critical incidents.

Provide clear training for all personnel and contractors on radio functionality and limitations.

Establish a failsafe protocol for verifying and responding to emergency alarms that includes manual confirmation.

The safety of personnel on-site depends on reliable communication. The current radio setup undermines this, and we urge a review before an incident highlights these flaws with serious consequences.

TITLE: Emerson Product Safety Notice - MAL Drains Fasteners
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
IMPORTANT PRODUCT SAFETY NOTICE
Incorrect Fastener Plating Impacting High Temperature Applications
Shipment Date Range: September 2021 – December 2024

This Important Product Safety Notice (“Notice”) is to advise you that Sempell GmbH (“Sempell”) has confirmed that fasteners used in a limited quantity of valve assemblies and also sold as replacement parts did not meet Sempell plating requirements. The bolting supplier’s EN 10204 3.1 and 3.2 inspection certificates incorrectly stated the components were zinc-plated, however, it was recently discovered that cadmium-plating was used instead. If installed in a high temperature application, the cadmium-plating could cause the fastener to embrittle and fracture. The cadmium plating may also be transferred to components in direct contact with the fastener. IF OPERATED IN APPLICATION CONDITIONS THAT CAUSE THE BOLTING TO EXCEED 232°C (450°F), THE BOLTING COULD FRACTURE RESULTING IN PROCESS LEAKAGE, SERIOUS INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. Our records indicate fasteners with the incorrect plating were supplied to you as part of complete product assemblies or replacement parts. The orders impacted by this Notice are identified in the attached Applicable Customer Orders section.

Uniper PO4500737738/600/5904.

TITLE: Non-Compliance with Respiratory Protective Equipment Requirements - GMI SHE 021
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An initial review of our Compliance with GMI SHE 021 subsequent to a question being raised in regards to WSC Ammonia Dosing Procedure for Units 6 7 8 has been conducted by myself. 

Within the above GMI it highlights the requirement for RPE to be worn in accordance with the aforementioned procedure and the MSDS. It highlights a number of statutory requirements in regards to RPE:

Requires employers to provide and maintain suitable, CE/UKCA-marked RPE for employees exposed to hazards. 

Employers must conduct risk assessments to ensure RPE is adequate, carry out fit-testing for tight-fitting masks, train users on proper selection, use, and maintenance, and store equipment correctly

However, the following gaps have been identified via documentation review, discussion with staff and process review on our wider Respiratory Protective Equipment Compliance, which is a statutory bound duty under the PPE Regs & the COSHH Regs :

There is currently no reference to RPE Within our Skills Matrix – thereby no face fit testing or  practical general training on how to wear RPE. Nor, how to maintain RPE

No Face Fit Testing Conducted in 5 years (It is required by the RPE ACOP to be conducted every 2 years)

RPE not officially inspected in the past 5 years (Should be inspected on a monthly basis) PM hasn't been completed since March 2020 

Inappropriate storage of RPE / Filters – filters are all out of date

Individuals whom have not been face fit tested have conducted tasks requiring RPE to be worn

TITLE: Manifold left in wrong state
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During commissioning activities the GT failed to come online due to a manifold for a pressure transmitter being left in the wrong state following calibration.

The GT sequencer test opens the gas SOV valve (GRA-71-MBP-43-AA003) and looks for a pressure spike on the outlet pressure transmitter (GRA-71-MBP-43-CP001) before reopening the SOV. The pressure transmitter's manifold was left with the isolator shut and the vent open post calibration, due to this the sequencer did not see the pressure spike and therefore did not reopen the SOV.

TITLE: Unsafe and unapproved electrical installation found on Safety walk.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the HESAC inspection of the Fuel Oil Compound today, a member of the electrical team noticed a damaged 110v extension plug & socket on the floor. He followed the cable back to where he assumed it would be plugged in, and noticed that it went through a hole in the wall of the old Mill Workshop. 

The cable was then strewn between several fuseboards and terminated directly into the 110v fuseboard by the roller shutter door. It was noticed that the live (brown) wire was terminated into the fused neutral busbar and the neutral wire (blue) was terminated into the fused live busbar. The opposite end of the extension lead was left with a plug hanging over a cable tray at the top of the bund access stairs and dangling, submerged into oily water.

The fuses were removed and caution notices applied to make the extension lead electrically safe, before removing the plug from the water.

The extension lead will be planned to be removed fully from the supply, then disposed of accordingly.

Unit 61 had B Inspection scope carried out as per TIL2469R2 recommendation. The PAUT of Weld AIJ3 detected low amplitude embedded indication close to the bore with a 2 mm cross-section and 548 mm long. PEM120 access control protocols for Unit 71 LP OTC are extended to Unit 61 prior to return to service. The Unit 61 Weld AIJ3 should be re-inspected after no more than 4,000 hours or 90 starts, whichever is sooner, following return to service from the August 2025 outage. At that time, it would be prudent to re-inspect Welds AOJ2 and AOJ3 to confirm the stability of the defects detected in these welds.
U61 Indication detail:
• AIJ3 (Alloy 800 to P11 transition weld): FDPI – no recordable indications. PAUT detected low amplitude embedded indication close to the bore (probably bore emergent) with a 2 mm cross-section and 548 mm long, observed previously during the 2024 monitoring exercise, but now recordable due to a higher amplitude response.
• AOJ2 (P11 to Alloy 800 transition weld): FDPI - 4-off surface breaking intermittent circumferential weld defects detected. PAUT detected a 2.5 mm deep surface breaking response close to P11 fusion boundary intermittent full circ. NB: no defects detected during previous monitoring of this weld.
• AOJ3 (Alloy 800 to 304 SS transition weld): FDPI - 4-off surface breaking intermittent circumferential weld defects detected during FDPI. PAUT detected a 2 mm deep embedded response close to the 304 fusion boundary with a 2 mm cross-section intermittent fully circ. & located 3 mm below the external surface. NB: no defects detected during previous monitoring of this weld.
General - Unencrypted
Surface replicas have been obtained from the surface breaking defects detected during the FDPI of Welds AOJ2 and AOJ3. These defects were located wholly in the weld metal and appeared to be intergranular and are probably fabrication flaws, associated with shrinkage, due to micro-segregation during welding. The PAUT responses detected on Welds AOJ2 and AOJ3 were not entirely consistent with the FDPI report and it is also not understood why these flaws were not detected during the previous inspection of these welds last year. Currently, it is considered that these flaws are unlikely to developing in-service.
For Weld AIJ3, the location of the flaw, and the increasing amplitude response, is consistent with the initiation of creep cracking we believe to be responsible for the failure at Keppel and it is in a similar position to the defects we are monitoring in the equivalent welds on both Units 71 and 81.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

PEM120 access control protocols for Unit 81 LP OTC are extended to Unit 71 prior to return to service. With concerns about the potential for high growth rates, it is recommended that Unit 71 Weld AIJ3 be re-inspected after no more than 2,000 hours or 45 starts. If the defect it is found to be developing more slowly than anticipated when Weld AIJ3 is reinspected, future monitoring intervals may be extended to circa 4,000 hours or 90 starts.

It could grow inwards to the bore surface, as well as outwards, quickly forming a large defect. The location of the flaw is consistent with the cracking mechanism believed to be responsible for the failure at Keppel and is in a similar position to the defect we are monitoring in the Unit 81 Weld AIJ3.

TITLE: Shortcomings in general safety management found during task audit.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A task inspection on civil works highlighted a number of shortcomings:

1. **RA225 Compliance**: It was noted that RA225 was not adhered to during the operations. This issue has already been discussed with the working party.

2. **PPE Concerns**: One member of the working party was seen wearing short-sleeved work wear. Long-sleeved work wear has since been obtained to address this.

3. **Glove Standards**: The working party was not aware of the minimum glove standards required for the tasks at hand. This has been explained to them.

4. **Lifting Area Safety**: It is recommended that the lifting area be improved with brick guards.

4. **Lifting Equipment**: A general-purpose builder’s bucket was used as a lifting attachment to transport mix from ground level to the plinth over the guard rail using a gin wheel. This practice should be reviewed. And was not covered in the RAMS

5. **Tool Safety**: The use of a fixed blade knife to trim expanding foam was not included in the risk assessment. This point needs to be addressed to ensure compliance.

6. **Circular Saw Assessment**: I advise that the use of a circular saw be specifically assessed in the RAMS rather than a general guideline such as "only choose the correct tool for the task."

TITLE: Work Areas set up during outage without Correx Sheeting
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During U71 Outage it was picked up on a safety walk that multiple work areas had been set up without the use of Correx sheeting - this is below expected minimum standard.

Two work areas specifically

HP Steam Pipework - De-Lagging causing loss of containment of insulation material / loose fiber debris falling between scaffold.

Condensers - Cleaning activities causing loss of containment of loose mud.

Both instances resulted in the work areas having an increased working from height risk which is mitigated by the correx sheeting being made available

When speaking to both supervisors of each working party there was a perception the Correx Sheeting wasn't available for work area set up. When investigated we had approx 150-170 sheets on site in the stores.

TITLE: Loss of DCS readings and control
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 02:23, a series of I&C alarms appeared on the DCS alarm page. Almost immediately, all DCS values were lost, signals turned bad, and no changes could be made, resulting in a complete loss of Unit control. This lasted approximately two minutes and at this time the Unit was operating at full load. Because we were unable to adjust the load, the unit was declared inflexible and SEL to MEL.
Once control was restored, a decision was made to deload the Unit to SEL and maintain its inflexible status until further guidance was received. The Production Day Team Leader and ROM's were contacted for support. Although the ROMs couldn’t access the system remotely, they provided assistance over the phone. Despite their efforts to diagnose the issue, they were unable to identify a cause, or determine if the issue might reoccur.
As a precaution, the decision was made to keep the unit inflexible at SEL until Engineering/ROM's could complete a thorough investigation.

The Production Day Team Leader and ROM's were contacted for support. Although the ROMs couldn’t access the system remotely, they provided assistance over the phone. Despite their efforts to diagnose the issue, they were unable to identify a cause, or determine if the issue might reoccur.
As a precaution, the decision was made to keep the unit inflexible at SEL until Engineering/ROM's could complete a thorough investigation.

TITLE: W14 - 04.2019. False fire alarm at maintenance transformer
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Contractors were carrying out general cleaning duties on the maintenance transformer (10BBT01) where they wanted to use pressurized air. There is a vertical pipe located on the wall next to the transformer which is part of the built in fire fighting system. The pipeline marked with grey label (grey = air) has completely similar marking like other pressurized air supply connections around the power plant. The pipeline on the wall is designed for firefighting system tests. The air in the pipeline is intended to support the fire fighting start mechanism at sprinkler heads. The pipe is not equipped with appropriate hose connection on it but the workers managed to connect to it. As they wanted to use the pressurized air whilst opening the valve the air has been released from the system which resulted in a fire alarm signal to local fire alarm control panel. As the fire fighting system is directly connected to the authority therefore they have also received the signal. According to their procedure the shift leader was called by the authority when the situation has been explained and the fire alarm disclaimed

TITLE: Valve incorrectly labelled
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A leak occurred on HRSG transmitter 01FSR54CFT, To identify leak it was required to shut away isolation valves as unable to get close to steam leak to identify. Isolation valves were identified on PID as 01FSRHV926 & HV927. Valve locations identified on plant and valves with these labels were closed. on closing 01FSRHV927 it was observed that 'A' transmitter was lost on DCS and leak did not stop. This valve was reopened and reading returned to normal on 'A' transmitter. In the area are all isolation valves for 'A' , 'B' and 'C' transmitter, some valves had no labels and by visually inspecting it was not clear which valves were pairs. It was possible to identify which valve was HV927 through process of elimination until leak stopped at flow transmitter 'C', valve label FSRHV927 removed from wrong valve (Label was actually around cladding adjacent to valve). It is unclear if all other valves are correct and will require further testing to ensure all labels are correct on all units (Valve locations slightly different on other units)

TITLE: SIS proof test valve slow to close
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Carried out a SIS proof test on Compressor 20. During this test was noted that the valve EKH201AA191 took approx. 5 mins to close. The test was repeated and the valve closed within 30 seconds (passed the proof test). To ensure this was not a reoccurring safety issue the SIS proof test was rerun. The SIS proof test was repeated and the valve once again failed to close. The unit was made unavailable whilst the fault was diagnosed and a faulty solenoid was found to be the cause. The solenoid was changed out and the valve tested numerous times with success.

Suffered a second drive failure on Gas Compressor 10. First occurred in December 2018 (synergi case no: 2661)

On investigation it was determined that the fault was again attributed to a fault 0.33µf snubber capacitor as per the initiating event on Compressor 20 only this time on an IGBT as opposed to a clamping diode. 

The capacitor in question was C1 on -G013A7 - MC2 IEGT Stack Phase W.

The drive didn’t trip and there were no signs of any further damage. The site fire & gas system detected smoke/heat and tripped the drive.

No injuries were sustained.

TITLE: Transferring - Offshore wind turbine
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A Trainer was attending a customer site to complete apprentice observations. He arrived at site on 22nd September and completed a successful transfer to and from the wind turbine. The following day the waves were high and RWE were in a position where they were deciding whether or not to go off shore. A decision was made to go ahead. Later in the day the team at RWE were told they had to leave the turbine within an hour and a half because the waves were getting high. The team transferred and all made it back to site safely however, Jonathan has described it as a frightening experience. RWE state safe wave height should be 2.8m but the waves on this day were over 3m. When they returned to site all RWE staff were asked to complete near hits so that they could investigate the reasons someone had authorised transfer to the wind turbine that day. As the Trainer was part of the group on site and for his own safety we wanted to raise this as a near hit within Uniper too.

TITLE: Boiler level switch faulty
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Heating medium boiler 10 was taken off line and drained for an upgrade project. As part of the recommissioning process, it was noted that the level switch was displaying as healthy, when the boiler had been completely drained down for the duration of the works.

The level switch exists to provide protection against low water level in the boiler and would trip the burner management system if a low water level is detected. It is part of the safety chain on the boilers which consists of the following; 3 pressure switches; 2 high, one low, 3 high temperature switches and the level switch.

TITLE: Spare gas regulator failed upon fitting
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The glycol regeneration units have a an integrated regulator/slam shut valve on the Natural gas line to the combustion chamber. The slam shut valve had activated twice so the unit was made unavailable by the shift team. A site engineer and mechanical shift technician inspected the unit and were unable to set up the regulator correctly to stop the slam shut activating. 

A spare was in stores so the unit was changed out. The new unit was tested and the engineer and shift tech were unable to set up the unit to factory specifications. The original regulator & slam shut was re-installed and the regeneration unit left as a poor spare. Wales & West were called in to investigate.

On 24.1.20 Wales and West attended site and repaired the original regulator that was fitted. 

They also attempted to set up the spare unit but failed. The unit was stripped down and a port that had been drilled out at the factory was found to be blocked with possible swarf; the internal measuring line on the attached diagram. The hole will be re-drilled by a technician.

TITLE: Incorrect paper work detailing type of radioactive NDT source planned to be used on weld testing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
NDT/Radiography has been completed on a number of shifts – the process involves completing the Appendix A documentation which details important information – one being the source type and size – the source decay certificate also states type and current size – the Appendix A is prepared by the FieldCore Mechanical contractor along with the decay certificate – this is checked/signed by the Uniper Engineer and distributed to relevant parties nominated on the Appendix A – the source nominated was Iridium - Ir192 23.7.
Iris the NDT company arrived at Enfield Power station at approx. 02:00 – after a review the Shift team leader found the source was a Selenium 75 Source with a strength of 32.8 Curies. (>20Curies) – The shift team leader has been on Nights since Wednesday, I was confident in the competence of the IRIS Engineers and decided this was admin error and not that IRIS had bought the wrong Source.
Once IRIS showed the shift team leader all the necessary paperwork for the Source, he allowed the Radiography to continue.
The fact that IRIS told him during the Saturday morning testing, that they were bringing a stronger Selenium Source for Sunday’s testing, was also taken in to account.

Descending from the bridge, I placed my right foot on the first downward step, and as soon as any weight was applied it slid out from under me. I was wearing rubber soled trainer shoes.
I was carrying a light lunch bag in my left hand.
With my other hand I held the handrail.
The steps were wet from overnight rainfall.

TITLE: PSO - Bulk caustic tank pressurising during delivery
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On opening the delivery pipework drain valve after a delivery of caustic to the bulk tank a significant build up of pressure was discharged into the delivery bund. If the drain valve had not been opened prior to the tanker driver decoupling from the delivery point there was the potential to spray any residual caustic over the driver. In addition, pressurisation of the tank will result in an increased risk of rupturing leading to loss of containment.

A previous occurrence of this pressurisation in October 2019 (notification 21307803) prompted investigation of the tank vent pipework which was found to be clear of obstructions.

TITLE: Unit 7 Safety Valve Lifting unintentionally
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U7 Steam Turbine was tripped using the CCR Emergency Stop Button as per the recommissioning programme for the HP bypass works.
The HP bypass opened satisfactorily but the IP bypass tripped almost immediately after opening, it tripped on Condenser Inlet temperature >Max 2; the spraywater valve for the IP bypass failed to quench the steam temperature in sufficient time. The Operator was unable to reset the temperature trip and therefore was unable to reinstate the IP bypass valve.
Subsequently, the CRH / IP systems pressurised causing the safety valves to lift.
Owing to the IP bypass trip, the GT PLS(T), leading to desynch at 03:04hrs. The HP header pressure increased due to the GT EV burners remaining in service for cooldown. Turning Gear was selected but the fires remained in service. The HP system safety valves lifted @155barg, the GT ESB was pressed at the CCR to extinguish the burners and reduce the HP pressure.

The IP bypass spray valve was later investigated by the maintenance team, I'm not sure what was found and if any changes to the control system were made.

TITLE: Power loss to site
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The gas processing plant suffered from total power loss, which caused the uninterruptable power supply to start. Site was in compression injection mode at the time and was in the process of bringing on a third compressor. 

The issue was caused by a faulty protection relay on feeder 2, this did not take the site offline as feeder 1 was still operational. However when the third compressor was being bought online the demand exceeded the current settings and an undetected latent fault on voltage transformer (blown fuse) of feeder 1 caused it to trip, leading to a power failure at site.

TITLE: SSoW - U4 pneumatic bled steam to DA valve 4002 permit for work ROMP
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Sunday 23rd May 2021, a Competent person (CP) collected a safety document PFW ROMP (Restoration Of Motive Power) to work on bled steam to de-aerator valve 4002.   Following collection of the safety document, the CP proceeded to the point of work he knew as 4002 valve, but found that the safety key issued with the PFW ROMP did not match the isolation lock on the valve, and there wasn't a ROMP notice present.  
The CP contacted the duty Senior Authorised Person (SAP) immediately to report his findings.  The SAP attended the point of work and found the CP on what he believed to be the wrong valve.  The CP confirmed through his experience and knowledge that he believed he was on 4002 valve, and showed the SAP a handwritten sign on the pneumatic valve control box (approximately 12ft away from the valve it's self) stating it was valve 4002.  The duty SAP took the CP to the valve that was isolated for the ROMP, and showed him the local permanent plant ID label attached to the valve stating valve 4002.  After some discussion and consulting drawings, it was still not 100% clear which valve was 4002.  The Duty SAP cancelled the PFW ROMP and de-isolated both 4001 & 4002 valves, and asked a Unit Operator to operate the valves remotely from the ovation soft desk in the main control room.  On operation of the valves it was confirmed that the permanent plant ID label attached to U4 4002 valve was incorrect, and that the valve was actually 4001.  

After confirming that the identification on valve 4001 (stating 4002) was wrong, 4002 valve was inspected and there was no plant label attached to 4002 valve, apart from the hand written sign on the pneumatic control box which is not local to the valve. 

U4 is currently on an Interim outage, and the air supply valves for both 4001 and 4002 were isolated at the start of the outage period (approx. 2 weeks earlier).  Both valves have been worked on through the outage with 4002 requiring setting up under a PFW ROMP before being returned to service.

Information

Both 4001 and 4002 pneumatic bled steam valves are located on U4 De-aerator.  On Unit 4, 4001 valve is located on the 'B' side of the De-aerator, 4002 is located on the 'A' side.  The valves are approximately 10 meters apart, each on it's own platform.  The valves are the opposite way round on U1 & U2 compared to U3 & U4.

TITLE: Loss of process control resulting in plant trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst withdrawing gas from the caverns and changing load from 700,000Sm3/hr to 900,000Sm3/hr by the pressure reduction valves (PRV’s) the plant suffered an unexpected Safety Instrumented System (SIS) trip on rate of change (falling <1bar/min) on the pipeline to the National transmission system (NTS).

In 2011 similar issues were experienced when certain plant conditions were met (approx. 8 bar dp between caverns and the National Transmission System [NTS] system). To prevent this from occurring a Management of Change (MoC) was implemented that allowed the shift operator control of the plant 'global gain'. This global gain effectively slows the plant control system down to prevent these large flow variances happening quickly and thus preventing demands on the SIS system. There is a standing operational instruction for the shift operator to manually change the global gain from 1 to 0.7 when in these pressure ranges.

On this occasion the operator had not reduced the global gain as when the withdrawal nomination commenced the conditions for the global gain to be reduced were not met, however, as these conditions are dynamic as the withdrawal nomination continued the conditions were met but the global gain was not adjusted.

Upon investigation of the DCS trend it appears this has been happening (to a lesser extent) for the past 16 months. This ties in with a rolling programme of overhauling each PRV, of which we have 3 off. It is thought that splitting the flow across two valves instead of three may have contributed to the issues described.

TITLE: Uncontrolled Release of steam via safety valve.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
It appears that U6 Sequencers (HRSG/WSC and ST) stopped running(Disabled themselves) when restarting the unit from an SSD trip during unit start-up. 
It was not noticed that the sequencers were not running initially (no alarms) until the operator realised that the HP bypass had failed to open. Immediately the HP by-pass was manually switched on which resulted in the HP-pass opening to pressurise the cold re-heat line as designed. This had the result of pressurising the CRH line due to high pressure already in the HP steam line. this consequently led to the CRH safety valves lifting at their designed lift pressures. 
Just after the HP-bypass had been switched on it was then noticed that the HRSG/WSC and ST sequencers were not running, these were immediately re-started. Once the condenser vacuum had reached 300mbar, the CRH pressure was able to relieve to the condenser via the IP by-pass valve. The unit the ran up as designed.

This had the result of pressurising the CRH line due to high pressure already in the HP steam line. this consequently led to the CRH safety valves lifting at their designed lift pressures. 
Just after the HP-bypass had been switched on it was then noticed that the HRSG/WSC and ST sequencers were not running, these were immediately re-started. Once the condenser vacuum had reached 300mbar, the CRH pressure was able to relieve to the condenser via the IP by-pass valve. The unit the ran up as designed.

On Saturday morning 15-Aug electrical commissioning of all boiler stop & bypass valves was undertook (ref. LWC 0249/SL BACTWAL) with B2 bypass vlv 114 being reported as "valve stuck". Outage permit office subsequently applied an isolation (inc. lock & tags to handwheels) to all BSV & bypass valves on Saturday pm. On Monday 17-Aug the Boiler engineer was informed of B2 bypass valve being tight by electrical team and this message was passed to valve contractor site manager to undertake further, non-intrusive, investigation. It was expected that the valve would be hand operated using handwheel only. On Tuesday 18-Aug the valve contractor confirmed they had adjusted valve packing and also decoupled the valve drive spindle to manually stroke the valve. While the current state of the boiler means there was no system derived hazard at this time, as a point of isolation, these works were not permitted at this time as no active safety document was available.

TITLE: No safe way for pedestrians to enter or leave site
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Is there currently any way to safely enter and leave site as a pedestrian? When I tried yesterday, one of the turn-styles was broken and the other was chained and padlocked closecd. There were no signs indicating how I could safely leave or enter site without walking on the road, which is not safe because the fence on either side leaves no off-road verge available for a pedestrian to move onto if cars are coming.

This doesn’t seem very safety first. At the very least, if the road solution is the intended way for people to enter/leave, surely there should be signs and a fence off walk-way to protect pedestrians? If it’s not, there should be signs telling people how they are intended to enter/leave on foot, since it wasn’t obvious at all to me.

If a pedestrian walkway cannot be fenced off, the turnstyle's automatic security should be disabled during office hours, and a security guard permanently stationed there.

TITLE: When is a Zebra Crossing not a Zebra Crossing
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There are two 'zebra crossings' marked on the approach road to UTG. Whilst one is associated with signage and orange beacons, the other comprises just the back and white road markings. This means that the pedestrian feels they have the right of way, but their safety is reliant upon drivers noting the road markings.

This was raised as an issue some 18 months ago and nothing appears to have progressed. I would suggest removing the makings, but keeping the drop kerb, In this way, the pedestrian knows to remain alert when crossing.

TITLE:
SSoW
Unit 3 hydrogen admission panel leak
CASE_DESCRIPTION: The working party were working in the Hydrogen admission panel performing leak repairs that were previously identified at the start of the outage. They attempted to carry out a leak repair on a small bore section of pipework and valve, this repair was to remove the valve, clean surfaces, replace components, rebuild and test. As the valve was being disconnected there was a loss of containment (suspected air), the working party quickly retightened the equipment and consulted with the SAP regarding their isolations. It is believed that the same pipework on all other units hydrogen admission panels is identified as white pipework and feeds a air filter/regulator. On this unit however the pipework is identified as red pipework which denotes this equipment to be part of the hydrogen system which the working party have documentation to work on.

TITLE: 20mm vent line pipework found disconnected
CASE_DESCRIPTION: Each heating medium boiler on the Holford GPP is supplied with gas at ~280mbar. Each gas supply has a small PRV that vents to a safe location at height. During a site tour, a Uniper employee noticed that the vent pipework had been disconnected on the downstream side of one of the PRVs. Hence, had the PRV of lifted, approx. 300 mbar gas would have vented into a cabinet (within a dsear zone 2 location) for a short period (a slam-shut valve would activate if the pressure continued to rise - isolating the release).

TITLE: BOP board changeover - loss of critical supplies
CASE_DESCRIPTION: A request was made to make available an 11kV VCB for routine maintenance. This required switching board supplies over. We opened 90BFT30 11kV VCB and the supplies changed over as they should. However, it soon became evident certain supplies had been interrupted. A power disturbance had resulted in loss of LV supplies to critical apparatus connecting the power station to National Grid. This equipment is UPS backed up. A further problem occurred with the MCW pump washing skid where another UPS failed. Throughout the whole incident, communications still remained with National Grid via phone.

TITLE: Damaged air hose repaired with electrical insulation tape.
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When setting up for Unit 3 LP ST blade inspection, which means use of pneumatic hand-barring equipment, found compressed air hose defect had been repaired with many wraps of insulation tape. Possibly twice! 
This equipment is fitted with bayonet fittings now which don't require the use of whip-arrestors, (air flow is blocked if hose is unintentionally released while at pressure) but if hose had detached from fitting completely this protective feature would not have worked. 
No opportunity to use alternative hose as this is a fixed installation with fittings not common with portable air hoses. 
Temporary repair such as this with unsuitable materials is storing up potential future injury.

TITLE: SIS Activation HAZID 83 - GRU 20 cooling air low pressure trip
CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There was a trip on GRU 20 caused by low cooling air pressure, < 10 mbarg on pressure transmitter QCA20ZP004 (HAZID 83).

The cooling gas is delivered by fan (QCA20AM050) via a control valve (QCA20AA116) which controls the GRU 20 combustion chamber temperature at around 910 degrees.

For over an hour before the trip the pressure downstream of the fan started to decline and the control valve opened to maintain the cooling gas flow / combustion chamber temperature.

The fan delivery pressure will reduce as the control valve opens and the back pressure declines. However, when the control valve is 100% open (during the start up pre-purge) the pressure normally reads about 20 mbarg.

This suggests that the control valve opened in response to a reduced fan delivery pressure (to control the combustion chamber temperature) rather than being the immediate cause of it.

TITLE: Lack of indication in control room that continuous monitoring of purge sample has been lost.

TITLE: CPU 2 Furnace ME-2-001 Therminol Pipeline Bellows expansion.
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During my routine rounds at 8:00 PM, a jarring noise was noted coming from the CPU 2 furnace area (ME 2-001). Upon inspection, it was determined that the furnace coil inlet piping had come loose from its supports. The pressure in the Pressure transmitter (PT-2-750) and the local Pressure gauge was found to be above the allowable range. Immediately, the CCR was notified, and the line was depressurized by venting. The inlet and outlet valves were opened and kept floated to the expansion tank (TK-2-005). The furnace was already in a shutdown state for 1 day for some other work on the burner assembly.

TITLE: CDC CW Purge pH reading low whilst purging to river
CASE_DESCRIPTION: During unit start up the CW system was put back into service with the purge valve to river opened and dosing systems reinstated. After some hunting the CW Purge pH reduced sharply to below 6.7pH at which point the purge valve started closing. The pH continued to drop over the next 30 seconds to below the permit limit of 6.5 to 6.35 and then recovered before the purge valve had time to close.  During this period the other 2 pH measurements on the system (at different points) remained as expected. Once all 3 readings were consistent the purge was opened again and dosing put into service.
